matches.title: Laron vs Candiotto
matches.tournament: ITF W15 Porto Velho (BRA) semifinal, outdoor hard
matches.headline: Laron had a rest day; Candiotto plays her 2nd match today after a 3-set QF grind
matches.analysis: W15 Porto Velho SF, outdoor hard, 20:00 local. Ranking says Candiotto (#457 v #842), but her 2026 doesn't back it: 23-15, with straight-set 1R losses to Gabriella Price (#863) and Luna Cinalli (#810) - players at Laron's exact level - and today she needed 6-3 5-7 6-3 to beat #1125 Sanchez Uribe on these courts. Laron beat that same Sanchez Uribe 6-4 6-2 last month and has lost one game in two Porto Velho matches. The clean, one-directional edge is scheduling: Candiotto's 2hr+ three-setter was TODAY, Laron's 45-minute QF was yesterday. Laron is also a 19-year-old lefty at a career high whose best 2026 results are all on hard (W15 Gaborone final). The counter is heavy and honest: Laron is 0-4 in 2026 versus players ranked #459-478 (Lan Mi x2, Gimbrere, Fullana), one set won in nine, and 2-5 in 2026 quarterfinals. Candiotto is home, more experienced, has a title this year. Genuinely close - I take the fresher, cleaner striker at a discount.

But it is closer than #383 v #516 looks: the week before, both made the Tianjin quarters, and Zheng's 7-6(4) 6-3 win over Morvayova (#300) beat anything Lu produced there. At three shared 2026 events — Anning (1,800m), Huzhou, Wuning 3 — Zheng went further than Lu. So Lu, but as a lean, roughly where the 1.61 price already sits.

matches.title: Kumasaka vs Borisiouk
matches.tournament: Phan Thiet 3 Challenger (CH, $63,000) - qualifying R1, outdoor hard, Phan Thiet, Vietnam (MD starts Sep 7)
matches.headline: Borisiouk's NCAA-SF level outruns his #1003; Kumasaka 1-5 and just lost to #767
matches.analysis: Qualifying R1 at the $63k Phan Thiet 3 Challenger, outdoor hard, ~11:10 local. Bookmakers 1.85/1.84 - a true pick'em despite a 455-place rank gap, because Borisiouk's #1003 is an artifact of ~20 pro matches a year while at NC State. Last November he reached the NCAA singles semifinals, beating #3-ranked DK Suresh (now ATP #353) 6-4 6-1 and #111 Max Dahlin; he was ITA #9 nationally and is now a full-time pro. Since June he is 14-3 with the M15 Wuning title (8-0 from qualifying), beat Agafonov (#618, career-high #465) 6-3 6-1 on Aug 6, and took CH-#426 Karan Singh to three sets in Astana qualifying. Agafonov had beaten Kumasaka 6-4 6-3. Kumasaka is 20-21 after 46-23 in 2025, 1-5 in his last six, and lost 3-6 4-6 to #767 Joshua Charlton six days ago. Against that: Borisiouk has not played since Aug 9, has one Challenger-level match all season, and Phan Thiet's 31C humidity slows the ball, blunting his 191cm serve against a 175cm grinder who lives on this circuit. A lean, not conviction.

matches.title: Singh vs Becroft
matches.tournament: ITF M15 Bali 03 (Amman Mineral, Series 4) FINAL, Bali Beach Country Club, Nusa Dua — outdoor hard
matches.headline: Higher-ceiling Singh hasn't dropped a set and crushed the man who beat Becroft here
matches.analysis: Coin-flip M15 final; I lean Singh on class. He's #604 (CH #388, #413 this season, 2nd seed at M25 level in April, Brazzaville Challenger QF in May) against a 25-year-old whose #679 is a career high set last week and whose only ITF singles title came a month ago. Singh has dropped no sets in Bali, conceding 24 games in 8, and beat Taguchi 6-3 6-3 — the same #947 who beat Becroft 6-4 3-6 3-6 at this exact venue on Jul 24. Becroft needed a tiebreak, a retirement and a set-down comeback (2-6 6-4 6-2, 1h59m vs Borg #533) to reach the final, and Singh arrives fresher off three weeks' rest. Against that: Becroft owns these courts — he won the M15 Bali title at Nusa Dua on Aug 2 and has played four weeks here — beat the best player in the draw, and is 39-21 this season to Singh's 21-19 (though most of Singh's losses are Challenger 1Rs playing up). No H2H and no public bookmaker line on an M15 final. A real lean, not conviction — hence no medal.

Andreeva: Kostyuk W 4-6 6-0 6-2 (Cincy Aug 19), Noskova L 5-7 in 3rd (Brisbane Jan). Anisimova: Kostyuk W 6-4 6-3 (Brisbane), Noskova L 1-6 4-6 (Cincy Aug 19).

matches.headline: Kostyuk's 2026 hard-court résumé dwarfs Noskova's; the Wimbledon loss doesn't transfer to NY
matches.analysis: Verified: US Open R16, Louis Armstrong 2nd match, not before 12:30pm ET Sunday (Sky Sports OOP; Kalshi's 18:00Z is a placeholder). Books 1.67/2.20, market ~57% Kostyuk. H2H 1-1, both 2026: Kostyuk 7-6(1) 6-0 on Madrid clay, Noskova 6-4 6-4 on Wimbledon grass; never on hard. The surface split explains both results: Noskova's flat first-strike game and serve (tour-leading 88 slam aces in 2026) peaks on grass, where she also won Berlin. On hard in 2026 she is 14-8 with no top-10 win and losses to McNally, Cirstea twice, Gracheva and Wang, all aggressive movers or counterpunchers, i.e. Kostyuk's profile; her Toronto first-serve % collapsed to 32% under pressure. Kostyuk is 15-6 on hard with straight-set wins over Anisimova, Keys, Alexandrova and Pegula, the flat-hitter type Noskova is, and lost only to Sabalenka, Rybakina, Swiatek, Gauff plus the AO ankle match. Transitive hard chains via Andreeva and Anisimova both point to Kostyuk. Kostyuk has dropped no set in NY (last three all under 90 min); Noskova blew a 6-2 3-0 lead vs Ann Li and needed 2h18 plus a doubles loss Friday. No current injury either side. Both chase WTA Finals points (Race: Noskova 7th, Kostyuk 9th). Weather mostly sunny 77F, light NE wind. Real edge but a 60/40 match, not more.

matches.title: Medvedev vs Tiafoe
matches.tournament: US Open R4 (round of 16), outdoor hard, Louis Armstrong Stadium, New York
matches.headline: Medvedev's return game has owned Tiafoe (6-0 on hard), serve is back; Tiafoe nursing issues
matches.analysis: Genuinely close, and the market (Kalshi 58%, tennisexplorer 1.63/2.27, Matchbook 1.71/2.40, hard-court Elo ~55%) has it about right. Case for Tiafoe: the best summer of his career (Cincinnati final beating Auger-Aliassime #4, Musetti, Nakashima, Tien), 40 wins in 2026, a dominant R3 (never broken, 85% first-serve points), home crowd on Armstrong, and recent same-surface chains that lean his way (he beat Nakashima, Damm and Tien within the month Medvedev lost to all three). Case for Medvedev, which I weigh slightly heavier: the matchup evidence is overwhelming and current-season, 6-0 in tour main draws on hard with one set dropped, including 6-3 6-2 in 61 minutes in January without facing a break point; his deep return and consistency turn Tiafoe's serve-forehand game into long rallies Tiafoe loses. His August slump (van de Zandschulp, Nakashima with 3 MPs, Damm) has visibly turned: 9-0 in sets here, broken once, big serving numbers vs Rinderknech. Tiafoe has had a cyst removed from his right wrist (Aug 8), a hip MTO in the Cincy final, withdrew from mixed doubles, played a 3h48 five-setter in R1, and on Sep 4 acknowledged he is managing physical problems and wants shorter matches; that is exactly the wrong profile against a grinder in best-of-five. Lean Medvedev ~59%, no medal: Tiafoe's form and the chains are real counter-evidence and Medvedev has folded from winning positions three times since June.

matches.analysis: US Open R3, third match on Grandstand Saturday (day session from 11am ET, so est. 2:30-3:30pm ET / ~19:00 UTC). Books: Zheng 1.66-1.68, Gea 2.21-2.26; Kalshi 57/43. I make it a near coin flip and lean Gea. The only direct matchup evidence favours him: 2-0 on hard this year, both times after Zheng won the first set (Noumea SF 4-6 6-1 6-4; Los Cabos R16 0-6 6-4 6-0 as a +154 dog). Gea is the higher-ranked player (#87 vs #107), is roughly 22-4 on hard in 2026 with an ATP title and wins over Lehecka, F. Cerundolo and Shapovalov, and closes matches brutally (6-0/6-1 final sets vs Zheng, F. Cerundolo, J.M. Cerundolo). Zheng's case is real: 81-83% first-serve points and 27/31 holds this fortnight, 22 aces, a home Grandstand crowd, and cool dry weather unlike the Los Cabos heat. Gea also showed variance, losing 3-6 1-6 to #163 Basavareddy in Q3 eight days ago. But Zheng's holds came against poor returners (Marozsan, Bu) and Gea returns far better. matches.title: Jovic vs Eala
matches.tournament: US Open R3, outdoor hard (Arthur Ashe Stadium, night session opener, roof available)
matches.headline: Jovic has beaten Eala three times in 2026 and her first-strike, serve-led game travels to hard
matches.analysis: US Open R3, Ashe night opener Saturday 7pm ET (23:00 UTC; Kalshi's 18:00 is wrong). Books have Jovic about 54% (-133/+107); rankings are near-equal (#14 v #18). The direct evidence points to Jovic: 2-0 this year with dominant margins, including 6-2 6-2 on grass at Queen's when Eala was in form (she beat Swiatek three weeks later), plus a 6-3 exhibition set on this exact court nine days ago. The mechanism repeats: Jovic takes the ball early, out-hits Eala from the baseline (34-15 and 26-12 winners) and attacks Eala's weak serve, while her own serve is clearly better (67% first-serve points won, 5 aces v Frech). Eala's 2026 hard-court ledger shows the same vulnerability to flat power righties: blown out by Noskova, Muchova, Bencic (4-6 0-6), Gauff, Alexandrova and Anisimova. The counter-case is real: hard is Eala's best surface (25-10), her DC title run over Pegula, Svitolina and Osaka gives her much stronger hard-court transitive chains, Elo favours her, and Jovic's summer hard results were soft (lost to #89 Korneeva and Bouzkova, 26 UE v Jones). Night conditions and an elite return help Eala too. Net: Jovic about 56%, a genuine but thin lean; no medal.

rows.analysis: First meeting. Milev (#866, born in Plovdiv, wildcard) is on the run of his life: he beat #300 Nesterov (last month's Plovdiv 2 finalist) 7-6(6) 3-6 6-4, Parisca 7-5 6-0 and #3 seed La Serna 6-3 3-6 6-1, all as a bookmaker underdog (4.03, 2.04, 3.34). Against that: Aboian (#431, lefty) is the far better player over the season (31-23 on clay, Challenger SF and three QFs) while Milev is 19-18 at mostly Futures level and lost R1 and R16 at the same venue in June and August (6-3 6-1 to #1137 Lazarov). Aboian's last two wins were dominant once settled (6-0 6-2 vs Sorger after a tiebreak, 6-4 6-1 vs Iannaccone who had beaten #2 seed Mrva). rows.headline: Cobolli: top-6 class, best-of-five format and a return that ate Blockx's second serve in Cincy
rows.analysis: US Open R3, Sat Sep 5, second on Armstrong after the 11:00 ET opener (est. 13:00 ET / 17:00 UTC). Books: Cobolli -110 (1.80-1.85), Blockx +100 (1.92-1.95). Cobolli (#6, RG finalist, Wimbledon QF, Cincinnati SF with wins over Paul #21 and Jodar #13) is the better player and the format helps him: best-of-five dilutes Blockx's serving streaks, and Cobolli is 13-2 at slams this year while Blockx is in his first slam third round. On faster Cincinnati courts Cobolli won 7-5 4-6 7-5 from 3-5 down in the decider; Blockx landed only 51% first serves and won 51% of second-serve points, and he was again at 51% first serves vs Trungelliti, so the second serve is there for Cobolli's return. Blockx has no top-30 hard-court win in 2026 (tour-level hard 3-4; his Madrid/Estoril surge was on clay), and NYC conditions (ace rate 8.7%, heavy humid balls, 83F day session) tilt toward attrition tennis. The honest counter: Cobolli has 6h55 on court from two slow-starting matches, calls himself 'slightly more tired', and in 2025 retired in this exact round after long early matches; Blockx is fresher, hit 27 aces in two rounds and was two points from beating him in Cincy. Net: Cobolli about 57%, no medal.

rows.headline: Fresher Bublik serving 80% 1st-serve pts, unbroken here vs Paul in 2025; ~41% vs 39c
rows.analysis: Third-round rematch of the 2025 US Open R3, when Bublik beat Paul in five with 22 aces and was never broken while Paul faded after a set-3 medical timeout. Books have Paul -200 / Bublik +154 (about 61-63% Paul), and Kalshi at 0.61/0.39 matches. Paul is the better 2026 player (38-16, Houston title, Delray/Hamburg/Queen's finals, Cincinnati QF with a match-point save over Zverev), returns far better (38% return pts won vs Bublik's 34%) and is the fitter mover in 85F heat. But Bublik is the fresher man: 1h22m to crush Mannarino 6-3 6-1 6-1 after a four-set win over Wolf, roughly 4h on court versus Paul's 5h45m (2h41m vs Wong, 3h04m vs Prizmic, where Paul won just 48% of second-serve points). Bublik skipped the whole North American swing so his body is rested, and he has won 80% of first-serve points in both rounds. Caveats: Bublik's two wins came against soft opposition (38-year-old Mannarino off a five-setter, Wolf back from shoulder injury), his hard-court level since February was poor (straight-set losses to De Minaur, Auger-Aliassime, Griekspoor, Hijikata, Berrettini), and Paul is 2-1 in ATP main-draw hard meetings. Net: market price is close to fair; I make Bublik ~41% vs the 39c ask, a thin lean on serve-driven variance, no medal.

Ebeling Koning (20, NED, #475 = career high) is on a genuine surge, 24-5 since Jul 5 with W75 Koksijde and W50 Oldenzaal semis, and beat #393 Kovackova 6-3 6-3 yesterday as a 2.28 dog, but her losses in that run came to exactly the tier Tubello sits above (Basiletti #267, Schunk #315, both in straights) and she is 1-2 vs top-320 in 2026. Ebeling Koning also played a SF in the Netherlands on Aug 29 then qualifying in western France on Aug 31. rows.headline: Cvetkovic's 10-1 run was all at 1,500m Verbier; heavy Serbian clay + doubles load
rows.analysis: Books have this 1.84/1.84 -- a true coin flip -- because Cvetkovic's maiden W35 title (Verbier, Aug 30, beating Okutoyi #488 and Strakhova #525) is fully visible against Martinez Cirez's four straight 1R exits. Two things the price doesn't carry. First, every match of that 10-1 run came at Verbier, 1,500m in the Alps: thin air, fast livelier clay that flatters her big forehand. Kursumlijska Banja is a ~450m Serbian valley -- heavy, slow clay, exactly where Martinez Cirez won all 7 of her ITF titles and reached the 2025 WTA125 Vic final (bt Tomljanovic 6-4 7-6(2), Cocciaretto 6-1 6-3). Second, the load: 12 matches in 16 days, a Verbier-to-southern-Serbia travel day Aug 31, a 3-set doubles Sep 1, singles Sep 2, doubles again at 15:30 today. Martinez Cirez has played twice in 15 days and skipped doubles. Common opponents lean Spain too. Cvetkovic is the better trajectory and is home; Martinez Cirez is the better player in these specific conditions with fresher legs.

rows.headline: Tan a class above at W50 level and a 2025 Leiria semifinalist; Johnson has beaten nobody inside #300
rows.analysis: Books sit at Tan 1.49-1.53 / Johnson 2.37-2.63 (Pinnacle 1.53/2.53, moved toward Tan from a 1.60 open), i.e. ~62% Tan. Tan (#216, CH #90) is the seed with the far better resume: W50 Croissy-Beaubourg title in March, RG/Wimbledon Q3R, Ilkley QF, and in July at the WTA125 Istanbul she beat Havlickova and Gasanova (#192) before retiring 1-6 0-1 down to Vandewinkel (~#100). She reached the Leiria SF on these courts a year ago. The knock is fitness and rust: the unexplained Istanbul retirement, a Prague withdrawal, then a single match in six weeks (6-4 6-3 loss to Stoiana, #122, who went on to qualify). Johnson (#459, 22, 6ft, ex-Old Dominion All-American) is match-sharp after two qualifying wins and a doubles win here, but her 2026 record is two W15 titles and a string of R1/R2 losses at W35+ level to Dolehide (#260), Hunter (~#190), Kaji (~#290), Liutova (twice), Arango, Rogers and T. Pieri; she has no win over a top-300 player. Shared opponents lean Tan (Tan 6-0 6-3 over Rogers; Johnson 1-1 with her). Cool, gusty conditions (21mph gusts, 20C) favor Tan's slice-and-variety game over a tall ball-striker. Fair ~64% Tan, but the Kalshi ask of 0.81 is well above fair on a $110-volume market, so size small. No medal: the retirement, layoff and Johnson's ledger are all on public results pages and already in the 1.50 price.

rows.headline: Home-clay coach with the better singles floor vs a doubles specialist riding three soft Q wins
rows.analysis: No bookmaker has posted a price (Tennis Explorer and Betexplorer both show no odds) and Kalshi's 6/80 and 13/89 quotes are placeholders, so this is a level read, not a value read. Deden is a 25-year-old Dutch coach with his own tennis school, #40 on the Dutch national list, who played Eredivisie league on clay this spring for Lauswolt (lost 6-0 6-3 to Robin Haase, a tight two-setter to Leimonias). His entire pro singles record is 4-3 in Haren/Alkmaar qualifying, but he beats unranked Dutch players routinely and was 7-6(7) 7-5 from Hendrikx (#2176) on these courts a year ago. He is a wildcard here (no qualifying played) and won doubles R16 Tuesday. Blando is a doubles specialist (#857, 5'11 140lb, spin serves, formation play) with a 5-18 pro singles record before this week; his three Q wins were a 10-7 tiebreak over a German who is 1-4 this year, a one-set retirement, and Waterbolk (#2087, 9-19 in 2026). He loses in straights to anyone ranked 1000-1750. Slow, damp evening clay after afternoon rain suits the home baseliner more than Blando's net game. rows.headline: Fresher Leong (~280 pts on court vs Matsuda's ~654) is holding serve; slight lean at 50c
rows.analysis: Challenger 75 R16 on outdoor hard, 2nd on Court 6 (13:30 local, 05:30Z); both came through qualifying. Matsuda (#483, 183cm, serve-first) owns the better season: three Futures titles since Jul 2025 and Challenger QFs at Samsun and Istanbul in Jul-Aug, and books opened him 1.57. But he has played ~654 points on three straight days in 30C/88% humidity: 267 points vs doubles specialist Uesugi (#1394 singles), broken three times by Meng (#1027), then 7-6 7-6 over Delaney (#365) converting 1 of 11 break points. His return won only 8-24% of return games this week and his second serve 32-55%. Leong (#551, 22) has played ~280 points: 6-0 ret, 6-1 6-4 over Palan (#506), then 7-6(3) 6-3 over lefty 8th seed Bar Biryukov (#288) while saving 7/8 break points and converting 3/4. Common opponents split (Leong better vs Takahashi/Dev/Shin, Matsuda better vs Samrej/Santillan/Sinclair), no H2H, though they were doubles partners at Bali M25 in Sep 2025 so nothing is a surprise. The line has already moved to 1.84/1.86 (Betfair 1.82/1.99), so the freshness gap is mostly priced; I make Leong ~54% on fatigue plus serve-hold form. Rain is forecast and a push to Thursday would reset Matsuda's legs.

transitive.summary: Chains split: Leong's 2026 wins over Takahashi, Dev and Shin (all Matsuda losses) vs Matsuda's wins over Samrej, Santillan and Sinclair (all Leong losses, mostly 2025). Cancel out.

rows.tournament: Zhangjiagang Challenger 75 (China) R16, outdoor hard
rows.edge_summary: Watanuki's Jul 5 walkover was a right-thumb (hitting hand) injury, Japanese press only; then 0-6 1-6, 2-6 4-6 and 33 idle days. Books rate a #420 at 43%. Tseng ~59% at 56c.

edge_factors.detail: Cary SF w/o Jul 5 was a right-thumb injury (tennis365, JP only); then 0-6 1-6 and 2-6 4-6 losses and no match Jul 29-Aug 31

rows.headline: Fit, in-form Tseng vs a #420 Watanuki with three 2026 breakdowns, in heavy humid air
rows.analysis: First on Central Court at 11:00 local (03:00 UTC; Kalshi's 06:00 is a placeholder). Fourteen books have Tseng 1.57-1.70 (vig-free ~57%), Kalshi 56c. Tseng (#221) is 11-3 in his last 14: Prague Challenger final (lost 5-7 6-3 6-0 to #186 Kumstat), then 6-4 6-0 here over WC Zhang (#845). Watanuki (#420, CH #72) is the more talented hard-courter (Indian Wells R16 in 2025, beat Tseng 2-6 6-2 6-1 indoors at Kobe last November) and served 8 aces at 83% first-serve points to beat #421 Pankin 6-3 7-5. But his body keeps failing: right-knee retirement Mar 3 and 2.5 months out, retirement at Prostejov Jun 1, right-thumb walkover from the Cary SF Jul 5, then 0-6 1-6 to Samuel, 2-6 4-6 to Matsuoka and no match for 33 days before this week. His 2026 hard wins are all vs #248 or worse; he is 1-4 vs top-250 hard opposition (only Ofner in Davis Cup). Conditions favor the grinder: 30C, 89% humidity, light rain, heavy slow air lengthens rallies, and Watanuki cramped in Tokyo heat last September. Common opponents on hard cancel out. Both are motivated (both named to Asian Games squads). Tseng ~59%.

transitive.summary: Hard-court chains cancel: both beat Wu, Burruchaga and Bellucci; both lost to Holmgren and Blanchet. Only clay chains lean Tseng (Boscardin Dias, Sachko), one with Watanuki hurt.

rows.title: Trotter vs Hsu
rows.tournament: International Challenger Zhangjiagang (CH75, China) R16, outdoor hard
rows.headline: Hsu is the real Challenger player here; Trotter is 1-9 vs top-350 foes in 2026 and lost the last H2H at his peak
rows.analysis: Zhangjiagang R16, first match on Court 6 at 11:00 local (03:00 UTC, not Kalshi's 06:00). Books have Hsu 1.56-1.58 / Trotter 2.2-2.32 (fair ~59% Hsu); Kalshi asks 0.63. Hsu (#268, CH 158) is a steady Challenger QF-level player: Winnipeg QF in July losing only to eventual champion Samuel (#110), an M25 Taipei title in August beating Dellavedova (#293), then R1 here 7-6(4) 5-5 when Ymer (#204) collapsed in the heat. Trotter (#464, CH 170) has cratered in 2026: he retired at Gwangju qualifying in April, missed seven weeks, lost two Futures matches in June, went 0-3 in Canadian Challenger main draws (Chidekh 6-1 6-2, Draxl, Zink), then sat out all of August before beating wildcard Cui (#454) 6-3 6-4 as a pick'em. His only 2026 win over anyone inside #350 is Matsuoka (#250) in Vancouver qualifying. H2H is 1-1, but Hsu's 6-3 6-3 Busan win came in Apr 2025 with Trotter at his career-high; Trotter's Yokkaichi 2023 win was on faster Japanese hard. Transitive chain via Moriya (Hsu won 6-2 6-3, Trotter lost) leans Hsu. Trotter has one extra rest day and a live serve (10 aces vs Cui), and Hsu has had bad losses (Gorzny #876, Mmoh), so 65% is the ceiling. No unpriced factor found: everything here is on public result pages, so no medal.

Only Saigo (Kaji 6-0 6-4; Ren split) leans the other way. Bookmakers have already flipped from Kaji 1.46 in Oct 2025 to Ren 1.58 (~58% de-vigged), so the form is largely priced; the surface switch and travel are the part I think the 60c ask still undersells. rows.title: Forti vs Clarke
rows.tournament: Como Lake Challenger R32 (Challenger 75), Como, Italy, outdoor clay
rows.headline: Clarke's class, clay pedigree and H2H win at a coin-flip price books make 52/48
rows.analysis: Official OOP: 3rd on Court 1 from 10:00 CEST (~11:30 UTC est). Books price Clarke 1.77 v Forti 1.92 (~52% no-vig); Kalshi is 50/50. The retail read — home Italian clay grinder v traveling Brit — inverts under research: clay is Clarke's BEST surface (189-102 career, 3 M25 clay titles in 2024, two at Santa Margherita di Pula), and he beat Forti 7-6(3) 6-3 on that same Italian Futures circuit in May 2023 when Forti was near his career-high level. Clarke's ugly 20-26 season is losses to top-200 players (Sakamoto #157 who then beat Muller, Chidekh #176, Kym #186 — all 3-setters); v #300+ opposition he mostly wins, and Forti is #363. Forti's comeback from a foot double bone oedema (#600 in March to #363) is real but Futures-padded (~8-9 Challenger MD wins); his last meeting with a Clarke-ranked opponent ended 6-1 6-3 to Cecchinato (#195) three weeks ago, and he retired from a Futures match Aug 18 before playing quali here. Forti's court time in Como and home crowd keep this close, but at equal 50c I side with the sharper book lean, class and H2H. Clarke ~53%.

rows.title: Breazu vs Misasi
rows.tournament: ITF M15 Arad (Romania) 1R, outdoor red clay
rows.headline: Career-high clay grinder vs 18yo on 0-5 slide with fresh mid-match retirement
rows.analysis: Both have been on the same Romanian M15 clay swing all August, so the comparison is unusually clean. Misasi (25, #859 = career high) made the Curtea de Arges final Aug 9, is 7-3 in his last 10, and his only losses are to better-ranked in-form players (Ghetu #625 as a 4.03 dog, ex-Challenger Madaras, title-winner Pieleanu #764); he routinely crushes lower-ranked youngsters (6-0 6-0, 6-1 6-2, 6-3 6-3 this month) — exactly Breazu's current profile. Breazu (18, #1268) is 0-5 in completed main-draw matches since Jul 24: he retired at 1-0 in the third vs Sciahbasi Aug 18 and, as a 1.50 favorite, collapsed 7-5 6-1 to Marinescu (#1065) Aug 25 — the same Marinescu Misasi handled 6-3 6-2 on Aug 6. Books (avg 1.71/1.99, ~54% vig-free) and Kalshi (53c ask) price this near a coin flip, apparently anchoring on the junior's pedigree; the joined-up chain and fitness pattern say Misasi is closer to 60%. Buy MIS at 0.53.

rows.title: Kulikova vs Yao
rows.tournament: ITF W60 Tianjin 5 ($60K) R1, outdoor hard, China
rows.headline: Kulikova holds W75 title form on hard; Yao slumping, twin Hontama chain says gap is real
rows.analysis: Market leans Yao (books 1.75 vs 1.87) on home Chinese hard, where she built her #282 ranking, plus a 7-5 6-2 H2H win over Kulikova at Shenyang last September. But Yao arrives off a 5-losses-in-7 German clay swing, beaten by #390 Schunk 6-0 4-6... incl. #504 McAdoo and #727 Wobker, and hasn't won a hard-court match since June 7. Kulikova's most recent tennis is a 5-0 W75 Lexington title run on hard (beat #293 Akli in the final) after qualifying into the Figueira WTA 125, where she beat #167 Hontama — the same Hontama who bageled Yao's second set six days earlier on Chinese hard and also beat Yao in Sep 2025. Both are 26/22-year-old lefties, so no handedness angle. Both come in rested (~3-4 weeks idle); Kulikova's 29-day layoff plus US-to-China travel is the main drag on her, Yao has been home since mid-August. Chains and current level favor Kulikova modestly; home comfort, surface base and H2H favor Yao. I make it a slight Kulikova lean at 53% vs a 49c ask.

transitive.summary: Twin Hontama legs (hard, 6 days apart in June) strongly favor Kulikova; only counter-chain (Belgraver) rests on a 17-month-old Kulikova loss. Net: clear Kulikova lean on comparable, recent, same-surface evidence.

He flew Sweden→Bali this week off that Aug 23 final — first hard court in 4 months, first tropical midday match since May. Style backs it: BB is a 196cm lefty, Leong 175cm right-handed, and Leong's season losses cluster against bigger hitters (Castelnuovo x2, Skatov, Shin 6-2 6-2). The market has already discounted BB hard (1.53-1.56, ~59%) for a poor month: 1R M15 loss to unranked Qian Sun 6-3 6-4 on Aug 26, a 6-4 6-2 Challenger loss to Cui Jie, a mid-match retirement Aug 4. That discount looks a touch too large: a #286 with a 2-0 same-surface H2H over a #551 qualifier should sit nearer 63-65%. Transitive chains are genuinely even (both lost 3-setters to Simakin, both beat Huang Tsung-Hao). Leong is sharper and heat-adapted (32C, humid) but plays a third straight day and his qualy wins came over #496 Palan plus a retirement.

transitive.summary: Only two shared opponents and both cancel: each lost a first-set-up three-setter to Simakin, each beat Huang Tsung-Hao in straights. Chains are too thin to move the number; the direct H2H carries it.

rows.analysis: Barki is really a doubles player (doubles CH #447, singles CH #1344, now #1921) with just three completed singles matches since July 2025. He returned from a wrist layoff at UTR PTT Bali on Aug 17, beat Thomas Patton 6-4 7-5, then withdrew from his next match on Aug 18 when the wrist flared again (Sofascore logs a walkover; antaranews and viva name the injury). He is a home wildcard here and also plays doubles R16 with Ellis the same day. Perez Ramos is #953, at a career high set Aug 3, 21-6 in singles in 2026 all on hard with two Futures finals and a SF, and he beat Shanker Heisnam - the #3 seed in this event's qualifying - 6-2 6-4 in May. He is ruthless against sub-level fields (6-0 6-3, 6-1 6-0, 6-3 6-3). Against that, he has not played since a flat Aug 4 loss to Coquelin at M25 Roehampton and must arrive into Nusa Dua heat and humidity from Europe, while Barki is acclimatised and has played this venue repeatedly. Rust and a home crowd are the genuine counterweights and ITF first rounds are chaotic, but the level gap plus a wrist that failed 14 days ago is the bigger fact. No bookmaker has priced this match at all.

rows.analysis: M25 Urayasu (SBC Dream Tennis, $30k outdoor hard, Chiba), R32, Sept 1. Lee is the 6th seed, #616, 17-16 in 2026 and runner-up at M25 Ma'anshan in April (l. Alastair Gray 2-6 3-6) — a genuine M25-level player. Katayama is a 37-year-old home wildcard, #1523, 170cm, Japan's domestic #41; TennisExplorer lists ZERO singles matches for him in 2026 and his last singles match was Matsuyama Challenger in Nov 2025. He entered three ITF events in Jun–Jul 2026 in doubles only; his last match of any kind was doubles on 8 Jul. That layoff, at 37, in Tokyo heat over best-of-three, is the biggest fact here. Against it: Lee retired hurt at 3-6 1-1 vs Shiraishi (#488) on 26 Aug and has retired 3-4 times in 2026 — but Taiwanese press confirms he then played doubles at the same event to the semi-finals, so the injury reads managed, not disabling. He also lost the only H2H (2017 Futures final). Taipei→Tokyo travel after a typhoon-compressed week is a real but small drag. Common opponents (Ochi, Hazawa) lean Lee. Lee ~70% — but at a 90c ask this is not a buy.

rows.headline: Gea's 2026 hard-court resume beats a clay-built lefty who is 1-3 in hard slam main draws
rows.analysis: First meeting, priced as a coin flip and it nearly is. Cerundolo (#45) is 42 spots higher but his ranking is clay-built: Bordeaux Challenger title, RG R16 off a cramping Sinner, and just 1-3 lifetime in hard-court slam main draws. On hard in 2026 he is 7-5, best win Rinderknech in two tiebreaks, and he was blown out by Ruud (1-6 2-6) and Auger-Aliassime (5-7 1-6). Gea is ~13-3 on hard in 2026 with wins over Lehecka (best-of-5 at the AO), Francisco Cerundolo and Shapovalov en route to the Los Cabos title, is 31-12 on hard vs 14-14 on clay at CH/ITF level, and is 2-1 vs lefties on hard this year. Against it: Gea played zero matches Aug 1-23, then lost the final qualifying round 3-6 1-6 to #156 Basavareddy on these courts serving badly, and best-of-5 in mid-80s humidity is the grinder's arena — Cerundolo has 8 tour hard matches in 17 days and elite stamina. rows.headline: Xiao is a 14-y-o junior ranked #414 in her first pro event, priced as favourite
rows.analysis: Final round of qualifying at W35 Kursumlijska Banja, clay. Karatancheva is the [7] seed, WTA #1339, 19, a clay grinder who has played this exact club 5+ weeks in 2026 (May, Jun x2, Aug W50, now) and went 21-19 on clay in 2025. Xiao is a wildcard with NO pro ranking: 14 years old (born 2012), ITF JUNIOR #414 (CH #391); her 2026 is J30/J60 titles in Asia plus first-round exits at J300 Pancevo and J200 Belgrade, and her ITF page lists hard as her preferred surface. Her one pro match, 6-4 6-3 over Kovgan [13], appears to be the whole basis for the market making her favourite - but Kovgan is a weak benchmark (no singles rank; 0-6 5-7 to Sacco, 1-6 3-6 to Viriant this summer here). Karatancheva beat Borovinskaya 6-3 6-1 on Aug 30 and is fresh (2 matches in 8 days). Against her: 11-12 in 2026 and 0-4 in second/final qualifying rounds (Stosovic, Ghirardato, Hageman, Lukas), so she is beatable by anyone competent. On slow clay a 19-y-o with 60+ pro clay matches over a 14-y-o debutante should be ~59%, not 45c.

transitive.summary: No shared opponents; chains are indirect. Both beat bottom-tier clay players this week, Karatancheva by the wider margin. Xiao's only pro data point is one win over a badly out-of-form opponent.

rows.tournament: Porto 2 Challenger (CT Porto Cup), CH75, final round of qualifying, outdoor red clay
rows.headline: Ayeni is the better 2026 clay player (9-6 vs 2-1) and ~200 ranking spots higher
rows.analysis: Both are in qualifying at Porto (clay, EUR97,640); Ayeni is Q5, Cacao Q12. The market has Cacao favourite (1.74 vs 1.98), which reads as a home-clay premium the data does not support: Cacao's own ATP bio says he 'competes primarily on hard courts', and his 2026 splits are hard 16-15, clay 2-1. Ayeni has played 15 clay matches in 2026 (9-6) across San Luis Potosi, Mexico City, Istanbul, Kosice, Prostejov and Bogota, has qualified into three Challenger main draws this year, beat Tomic at Wuxi and made the Temuco SF (Nov 2025) over J.M. Cerundolo and Kicker. Cacao's ceiling is an M15 title (his first, at 28) and he is 0-5 versus top-500 opposition since his Aug 2025 comeback; his 6-2 6-1 Q1 win came against an unranked national U18 champion in his second pro match. Ayeni won the only H2H. The offset is real: Ayeni is 2-6 in his eight matches before Porto, losing twice to #870 Brady as favourite. I make it Ayeni ~56% against a 48c ask - value, not a mispricing.

rows.tournament: Porto Open (CT Porto Cup) ATP Challenger, qualifying final, outdoor clay, Porto, Portugal (Aug 30-Sep 7)
rows.edge_summary: Schoen is 31-10 on hard in 2026 but 6-1 on clay, five of those in Swiss club league. First real clay test vs a man who played 30/30 matches on clay and made a Ch75 SF beating Dellien. Fuele ~43% at 39c.

rows.headline: Pure clay grinder vs a hard-court M15 specialist on his 3rd clay start of 2026
rows.analysis: Porto Open qualifying final, outdoor clay. Schoen is the better player on paper: 37-11 in 2026 with two M15 Kayseri titles and an M25 Figueira da Foz final. But every one of those results came on hard court - he is 31-10 on hard this year and 6-1 on clay, and five of those six clay wins are Swiss Interclub club-league matches. His only competitive pro clay in 2026 is a 5-7 5-7 loss to Poljicak (#345) at Zug and yesterday's win over Boris Arias, a #1541 doubles specialist. He has never won a Challenger main-draw match. Fuele has played 30 of 30 matches in 2026 on clay (125-79 career) and six weeks ago qualified into the Cordenons Ch75 semis, beating top seed Hugo Dellien and Thiago Seyboth Wild. The counterweight is real: Fuele retired at M15 Xativa on Jul 30, lost 5-7 0-6 to #1043 Gavrielides at Augsburg on Aug 23, and needed 2h+ over three sets yesterday while Schoen spent 65 minutes. That, plus 27C heat, makes Schoen a deserved favourite - just not a 63c one. I make it 57/43; Fuele at 39c is the side with the price.

Gueymard still owns the bigger weapons, an R16 on these exact courts in 2025 and a 7-6(4) 6-3 win over #152 Budkov Kjaer on 21 Jul, so this is close — but 43c is too cheap.

rows.title: Nikles vs Rottoli
rows.tournament: Como Lake Challenger (CH75) final qualifying round, outdoor red clay, Tennis Como
rows.headline: Nikles a level up - M25 finalist vs an M15 QF loser - and won the July clay meeting
rows.analysis: Qualifying final at Como (outdoor red clay, Tennis Como); winner enters the main draw. Nikles (#424, CH #256) is a genuine M25/Challenger clay grinder: M25 Castelldefels final in April, Mataro SF in May, Bucaramanga Challenger QF, 5-2 at CH75 level in 2026, 272-172 career on clay. Rottoli (#901, CH #403 back in 2023) has slid to M15 level - he lost the M15 Vienna QF 3-6 3-6 on Aug 28 and is 14-16 this year. But they met eight weeks ago on Moroccan clay at M25 Rabat and Nikles needed 6-7(3) 7-5 7-5, so the on-court gap is smaller than the rankings, which is why the price sits at 62c not 75c. Tiebreakers for Nikles: he beat Kasra Rahmani (#778) 6-2 6-4 on this exact court yesterday, and Rahmani beat Rottoli 6-4 6-2 on clay in April; and Rottoli played three matches in Vienna Aug 26-28, moved ~700km, then came from 1-4 down to edge La Vela. Offsetting: Rottoli was born in Como, this is his home event, and Nikles is 2-4 in his last six official matches. Fair near 67% - a thin edge on the 63c ask, not a medal.

Rankings are effectively tied - Tabacco ~#650, Kirkin ~#657 - and Tabacco is seeded [6] to Kirkin's [7], so the entry list itself rates this a coin flip. Tabacco also came through Q1 far more cleanly (6-2 6-1 over Shandarov vs Kirkin's 6-4 6-2) and is a clay-raised Italian at 20-14 on dirt this year. Bookmakers price Tabacco 2.11 / Kirkin 1.56 - de-vigged 42.5%, above Kalshi's 41c ask. I make it ~45%: Kirkin is the better player, but not by 19 points.

She has not played competitively in 19 days. Counterweights are genuine: Linette's ceiling is far higher (CH #19, 2026 wins over Swiatek, Alexandrova, Navarro, Ostapenko), quick NY hard suits her flat pace more than Jones's clay run, and the Wang Xinyu chain favours her. Near coin flip; Jones is simply the cheaper half at 0.49.

rows.analysis: Deciding qualifying round, W15 Tianjin, outdoor hard, ~33C, 10:00 local. Rankings favour Lee: #345 vs #401, Q-seed 2 vs 10. Lee is sharp and acclimatised - second straight week at this venue, 6-1 6-2 over Yuan (Q-seed 14) and 6-1 6-2 over Chanta (#460), then a comeback 2-6 6-4 6-1 over Ayano Shimizu (#401, CH #175) on this court yesterday. Sidorova is the better talent on paper - 2025 W15 title, Maanshan final in March, scalps of Lansere (#265) and Kaji at WTA level - and the transitive chains lean her way. She is also far fresher: one 55-minute win in a fortnight against Lee's five matches in six days including two three-setters. Offsetting that, Sidorova has played only three matches since 18 June and lost her last completed one, on Serbian clay, then flew to China. Book (2.23/1.58 = 41/59 normalised) and Kalshi (~39/61) both price Sidorova 58-60%. I make it about 56/44. That leaves Lee thin value at the 0.40 ask and Sidorova clearly overpriced at 0.62. rows.analysis: Genuinely close, and priced that way: books have 1.84/1.80 (49.5%/50.5% vacuum-stripped), Kalshi 0.51/0.58 asks. Tajima is the better player on paper — #1401 with a #603 career high, doubles #340 playing Challenger main draws weekly (Sion, Astana, Plovdiv, Samsun since late July), 34-25 in singles in 2025, All-Japan junior champ at 12/16/18U and 2018 Roland Garros boys' doubles winner, with serve as his stated weapon. Tanaka is unranked (CH #1513), 22, a pure M15/M25 qualifying grinder who is 9-6 on hard in 2026 but has never won above that level. Both won Q1 yesterday; Tajima's 6-3 6-3 over Matsui was cleaner than Tanaka's 7-6 6-4 over Katayama. Common opponents lean Tajima on margin (Inui, Yamamoto). Offsetting: Tajima's singles is now a sideline (13 matches, 7-6 in 2026, incl. a 6-2 6-1 wipeout by Yamasaki), he prefers clay, and he flew back from Europe on ~35C Tokyo Bay hard courts. Net a modest lean, not an edge — 0.55 at a 0.51 ask.

rows.analysis: Qualifying final, outdoor hard, Zhangjiagang CH75. Both had soft Sunday openers: Palan 6-4 6-3 over 32-y-o doubles specialist JiSung Nam (alternate, doubles #143), Leong 6-0 when WC Weiyi Kong retired after one set. They met 41 days ago on the same surface — Segovia qualifying final — and Palan won 6-7(6) 6-4 7-5 as the 2.12 underdog with Leong the 1.66 favourite; the book has now re-priced almost identically (Palan 1.96 / Leong 1.74 = 47/53). Palan is higher ranked (#502 v #543), 1.91m with the bigger serve and a #280 ceiling, and outplayed Leong across both shared July Spanish events (6 wins to 3). Against that, Leong owns the transitive chains: he beat Joshua Charlton 7-5 3-6 6-2 the day after Charlton beat Palan 6-3 6-2 at the same April ITF, and at Astana on Aug 10 Leong lost 4-6 4-6 to Arutiunian while Palan was beaten 1-6 4-6 by Pankin. rows.headline: Unknown home wildcard outrates the grinder: UTR 12.5 vs 11, and Venkataraman is in freefall
rows.analysis: Empty book (12/88, $0 vol) on an M15 Nonthaburi Q1 between an unranked Indian circuit grinder and an unranked Thai wildcard. Standard sites show only one side: Venkataraman has 60+ pro matches but is 24-39 career, riding three straight losses — Q1 blowouts in Taipei to UTR 12.46/13.01 opponents (2-6 1-6, 3-6 1-6) — and in 2026 he is 0-6 in straight sets vs anyone rated 12.4+, beating only sub-11.5s and one match-TB escape. Chinsupakul is invisible to TennisExplorer/Flashscore (pro debut) but UTR rates him 12.0 (3-mo 12.53) vs 11.0 (3-mo 11.75): he beat pro-circuit regular Noppadol Noikor (UTR 11.53, ATP-profiled, plays these Thai ITFs) 6-4 6-2 on Jul 3, won a Florida UTR title in June, and flipped his two 2025 losses to Noikor into a comfortable win — an 18yo improving fast, now at his home-district LTAT club in Pakkret/Nonthaburi. A 0.8-1.5 UTR gap maps to ~70-85% for the Thai; I discount for pro-debut nerves, an 8-week tracked-match gap, and a 'projected' rating at 52% sample reliability. Call: Chinsupakul 67%. Monsoon warning all weekend adds schedule variance, not side bias.

rows.headline: Marcinko winless on hard since Feb (3-11); Birrell 16-14 and won the hard H2H
rows.analysis: Both arrive cold — Birrell has lost five straight, Marcinko is 2-5 since Eastbourne — so this reduces to surface. Birrell is 16-14 on hard in 2026 (Adelaide SF, ATX SF, Austin 125 SF, wins over Cristian, Maria, Potapova, Tomljanovic); Marcinko is 3-11, all three wins in January, and no hard-court win since 1 Feb — roughly eight straight losses on the surface over seven months. The H2H is 1-1 but splits cleanly by surface: Marcinko won on Eastbourne grass 6-1 6-4 in June, Birrell won the hard meeting in Austin 0-6 6-3 6-4 after being bagelled in set one. The strongest chain agrees: Birrell beat Cristian 5-7 6-1 7-5 on Adelaide hard; Cristian beat Marcinko 6-1 6-1 in 64 minutes on Dubai hard. Fatigue is a wash — both lost Monterrey R1 on Aug 25 and flew to New York. Marcinko has the higher ceiling at 20 (peaked #45 in July, Rabat title) and won the most recent meeting, which is why this prices level, but on a medium-fast hard court the surface record is the biggest single differentiator. Birrell ~58%.

rows.title: Vandewinkel vs Pliskova
rows.tournament: US Open R1, outdoor hard, Flushing Meadows NY
rows.headline: Fresher and 2-0 vs a common opponent Pliskova lost to; big-serve risk keeps it thin
rows.analysis: US Open R1, outdoor hard. Bookies 1.89/1.92 (de-vig 50.4/49.6) match Kalshi's 50c — a genuine coin flip. Vandewinkel (#77, career high, 22) arrives 13-3 in 16 matches since Wimbledon: W100 Landisville title (beat Zakharova #81 in the final), a Cincinnati qualifying run, and a competitive 4-6 3-6 loss to Wang Xinyu. Pliskova (#56, 34) has played three matches in seven weeks, going 1-2, and won four games in her last two. Common opponent Zakharova favours the Belgian 2-0 vs 0-1. Pliskova's 2024 ankle rupture (all ligaments, both tendons, two surgeries) worsened an already-known movement weakness, and NYC heat suits younger legs. But I disproved the obvious edge: those 6-0 6-2 drubbings came from Mirra Andreeva (top-5) and Sara Bejlek in the week Bejlek beat Krejcikova, Alexandrova and Sabalenka to reach the semis. Pliskova's 2026 tour-level body of work (21-12, wins over Anisimova and Alexandrova) outclasses Vandewinkel's ~4-10 in tour main draws, and the Belgian is 0-3 at slams chasing a first main-draw win. Serve pedigree keeps this near even. Thin lean only.

rows.title: Oliynykova vs Brantmeier
rows.tournament: US Open R1, outdoor hard, Flushing Meadows NY
rows.headline: Market prices the NCAA-champ wildcard like a peer; the tour-level record says otherwise
rows.analysis: US Open R1, outdoor hard. Oliynykova is #46 (career-high #44 this month) with real 2026 tour scalps: Eala, Putintseva, Wang Xinyu, Bondar, Sherif twice, RG R3, an Antalya 125 final on hard, 18-10 on hard. (Her Tauson 'win' in Rome was a 3-1 retirement - discount it.) Brantmeier is #425, career-high #411, three months into a pro career after the NCAA title, in via the collegiate WC playoff. Her 2026 pro ledger is ITF-heavy and 1-4 vs top-200: lost to Shymanovich (#205) 4-6 3-6, split with Mandlik (#170), lost to Vandewinkel (#99), pushed Yuan Yue to three in Miami qualifying. Clean chain: Oliynykova beat that same Shymanovich 7-5 6-1 on hard in March. Fifteen books incl. Pinnacle (1.96/1.93) make this a pick'em - heavy respect for the college narrative and home crowd. Counterweights are real: Oliynykova withdrew injured twice in 2026 (May thigh, July Hamburg), is in week four of travel via Monterrey, and gets bageled by big hitters (0-6 0-6 Kessler, 1-6 0-6 Andreeva). But Brantmeier has zero Slam main-draw singles matches and no match since Aug 8. I make it ~60/40. Everything here is public, so no medal.

rows.analysis: Market has Ostapenko ~60% (books 1.58/2.37), matching Kalshi's 61c. That discounts her slump, but not enough. Ostapenko hasn't won a match since Jul 1 (Wimbledon R2); her whole US Open hard prep was 4 games won — retired 0-6 0-4 vs Zhang Shuai (illness) in Toronto, then lost 6-1 6-3 to Frech in Cincinnati with 13 double faults and 42.9% first serves. She has retired mid-match three times in 2026 (~8% vs ~2% tour baseline) and Kalshi settles a retirement as a loss. Maria leads the H2H 2-0 and led the last meeting 6-1 before Ostapenko quit; her slice/no-pace junkball wrecks Ostapenko's timing, and 16 days ago she dismantled Yastremska — the nearest stylistic analogue — 6-1 6-2 in 72 minutes on hard. Against that: Maria is 5-12 on hard in 2026, has never passed R2 in 10+ US Opens, and hard court is where Ostapenko's power finally gets through the slice. That is real and it is why Maria is the dog. But 39c prices her as a no-hoper. She isn't. Fair ~43%.

rows.headline: Ito won 6-0 6-7 6-4 on hard 4 weeks ago and is 4-1 in opening matches; 39c is cheap
rows.analysis: Ito's #369 badly understates her. She entered on a protected ranking of #88 - HIGHER than Selekhmeteva's #98 entry rank - after a lumbar stress fracture cost her Sept 2025-Feb 2026; career high #82 last August with a win over then-top-10 Paolini. Four weeks ago on the same North American hard swing she beat Selekhmeteva 6-0 6-7(8) 6-4 in Toronto qualifying as a 2.82 dog, and eleven days later blitzed Sierra (#88) 6-1 6-1 in Cincinnati. The Vandromme chain agrees. Crucially, Ito's 12-20 season is a first-match/second-match split: since July she is 4-1 in the opening match of an event and 0-4 in the follow-up - consistent with a back returnee who fades on back-to-back days. This is an opening match. Against that: Selekhmeteva has the far higher floor (AO 3R over Badosa, Wimbledon 2R), is match-sharp off three Philadelphia wins, and was 23 days cold when Ito beat her. Bookmakers price Ito 2.31 (~41% devigged) versus a 39c Kalshi ask - the sharp cross-check is on the same side.

rows.headline: Gibson's hard-court season vs a Vekic who has lost 4 straight from a set up
rows.analysis: US Open R1 on outdoor hard - the surface that defines both seasons in opposite directions. Gibson is ~22-8 on hard in 2026 (3-6 clay, 2-5 grass); as a qualifier she beat Paolini (#7), Alexandrova (#11), Tauson (#17) and Osaka to reach the Indian Wells QF and Miami R16, then made the Toronto 3R beating #18 seed Chwalinska and pushed Sabalenka to a second-set tiebreak. Vekic's 2026 peaks are grass (Queen's title over Raducanu) and clay (Istanbul title, RG win over Osaka); on hard she is around .500 or worse and has lost four straight - Krueger, Golubic, Wang Xinyu, Parry - winning the opening set in every one and taking just 12 of 36 third-set games. At 30 with a knee-surgery history, in NY heat, that fade pattern matters against a 22-year-old. Common opponents split cleanly: Vekic's edges (Pliskova, Bouzkova, Jeanjean) are all grass or clay; the hard-court chains favour Gibson. The market is a coin flip, which prices most of this - but Gibson's price is dragged by a loss to Cabrera (#289) in a WTA 125 tune-up five days out.

rows.analysis: US Open R1, outdoor hard. Parry (#50) is in the form of her life - 6-1 on hard in August, beating Dolehide, Mertens, Boisson, Vekic, Tauson and Li to reach her first career WTA final at Monterrey, which she plays tonight at 23:30 UTC. That is the problem: 8 matches in 17 days, a title match ending near midnight ET Saturday in Mexico, then travel to New York for a Monday R1. Golubic has not hit a competitive ball since ~Aug 14 (Cincinnati R2, a 3-hour loss to Tjen) and owns the H2H 2-0, both straight sets - 6-1 6-3 at Ilkley 2025, 7-5 7-6(6) at Cluj 2022. Bookmakers (2.04/1.77 = 46.5/53.5) and Kalshi agree, so the fatigue is already priced. I make it a true coin flip, so 46c on the rested veteran is the better half of a fair market - not an edge worth a medal.

rows.title: Giron vs Buse
rows.tournament: US Open R1, Flushing Meadows, outdoor hard (best-of-5)
rows.headline: Buse beat a #51-#93 field on these exact courts; Giron lost R1 there to a #394
rows.analysis: Buse (#34) is the better player right now and proved it on these exact courts: at Winston-Salem he beat Walton (#93), Altmaier (#65), J.M. Cerundolo (#51) and Bonzi to reach the final, while Giron (#77) lost round one there in about an hour to lucky loser Dhakshineswar Suresh (#394). That caps a wretched hard swing for Giron, also beaten by 17-year-old Cruz Hewitt (#612) in Washington and Rocha (#125) in Cincinnati qualifying, with no ATP hard main-draw win since Indian Wells in March. Buse won their only meeting 3-6 7-5 7-6(8) at Queen's, though Giron held three match points. Passaro is live: 3-0 in qualifying without dropping a set, and #207 badly understates a career-high #89 derailed by a February wrist microlesion and his father's death in May. Best-of-five breaks the tie: De Jong is 2-0 in five-setters in 2026 and beat Passaro from two sets down at RG 2025, winning the fifth 6-1 in 3h49m. Common opponents lean the same way. rows.analysis: US Open R1, outdoor hard, mild (~80F). Machac (#62, CH #20) tore a left foot muscle at Roland Garros, missed the entire grass swing and Wimbledon, and sat 79 days. Since returning he lost 3-6 2-6 to Carreno Busta (Cincinnati, Aug 14) and 2-6 6-7(1) to #389 Mees Rottgering (Winston-Salem, Aug 25), who had never won a tour-level match: zero sets won in two matches, his worst loss by ranking since 2023. He also retired mid-match at Montpellier in February and withdrew from Rome in May, so 2026 is a pattern of breakdowns, and best-of-five on hard is the harshest test of that foot; a retirement settles as a loss. Samuel (#110, career high this month) is at his peak: Winnipeg Challenger title in July without dropping a set, then three qualifying wins on these exact courts, two days' rest. Caveat: Machac's class is real (Adelaide title, wins over Tsitsipas, Dimitrov, Paul) and Samuel has never beaten a top-70 player in a completed match. rows.analysis: Two players ranked #36 and #37, so a 52/48 market is honest — but three things lean Fery. (1) They have met: Fery beat Buse 6-3 6-1 in 67 minutes on indoor hard (Stockholm qualifying, 11 Oct 2025) when Fery was #230 and Buse #108 — a compact flat counterpuncher overwhelming a clay-bred topspinner. (2) Surface: Buse's 2026 tour-level hard record was 0-3 entering this week (4-3 now, all four wins here); he is the first Peruvian in an ATP hard final since 2004, and his title came on Hamburg clay. Fery is 6-3 on hard, 8-3 on grass, beat Cobolli and Dimitrov at Wimbledon and took De Minaur to 7-5 7-6(3) in Cincinnati. (3) Legs: ~5h35 on court this week vs Buse's ~8h after Duckworth's 59-minute retirement, in mid-80s humidity. Against that, Buse beat much the better field (Walton, Altmaier, JM Cerundolo, Bonzi) while Fery's half of the draw collapsed, and Buse already owns a trophy. All of this is public and priced, so no medal — but 53c is a shade cheap.

Castelnuovo is #455 (CH #342 in May), a Challenger regular playing down: he won M25 Maanshan in April beating Santillan, and yesterday beat Yanki Erel (#346) 6-4 6-4, the best win either man has here. Chen has no ATP singles ranking at all ($1,815 career prize money, ITF junior #16) but is 3-0 this week without dropping a set: Matsuda 6-3 6-0, Jasika (#402) 6-4 6-3, Hyeon Chung (ex-#19, ~#500) 7-5 6-0. Those are real scalps, which is why the price is only 55/45. I discount them modestly: Jasika was on his 9th match in 16 days and third straight event, and Chung is a 30-year-old comeback veteran who folded 6-0. The structural read favours Castelnuovo: a 1.88m lefty with a one-hander serving at a 1.67m/58kg junior on hard, 29 vs 18, and at the same M25 Maanshan in April Castelnuovo took the title while Chen lost R1. Both are left-handed, so neither gets the usual lefty edge. Chen is on his fifth straight match day; Castelnuovo had 18 days rest and scratched from doubles to protect his legs. I make it ~60/40, a small edge on the 57c ask, not a mispricing worth a medal.

H2H is 1-1 but split by surface: Mertens won the hard meeting 6-0 6-4 (AO, Jan) with 8 aces, 69% first serves and 61% of total points; Bartunkova's 6-1 6-4 win came on Berlin grass, where Mertens made 52% firsts, 7 DFs and won only 30% of second-serve points - a grass-specific serve collapse that doesn't transfer to hard. Fatigue is the live differentiator: Bartunkova has ~7h on court in five days, including back-to-back 2h45 and 2h44 wins on consecutive days, with 8 double faults and 11 break points faced against world #90 Vidmanova. Mertens has ~3h30, her QF lasting 1h28. Against the tour's best rally-extender, a leaking serve on tired legs gets punished. Against that: Bartunkova is at a career-high #38, beat Tauson and Andreescu on hard this month, and Mertens hasn't beaten a top-40 player on hard since February. But the market has already repriced Bartunkova from 3.70 to 2.17 in this exact matchup since January - her rise is priced in. Thin lean to the fresher, better hard-court server.

rows.analysis: W15 Pécs semifinal on outdoor clay, first match on at 10:00 local (08:00 UTC, per tennisexplorer and betexplorer; Kalshi's 14:00 is a placeholder). Senica (#708, 18, seeded 4) is the better and rising player: she won W15 Rogaska Slatina in August, owns 2026 wins over #342 Zelnickova and #394 Tsygourova, and has won 8 of her last 9 W15 main-draw matches. Her floor is real though: she lost to #1012 Mpetshi Perricard two weeks ago, needed 7-5 in the third vs #913 Andrienko here, and gets blown out by #400-650 players. Mrazikova (#1289, 22) is having the week of her life, beating top seed Grubor (#515) 6-4 6-1, but five weeks ago she was losing W15 qualifying to an unranked player, and she lost 4-6 2-6 to #713 Sziedat, exactly Senica's band, in July. Common opponents lean Senica (Hrdinkova, Meyer auf der Heide, Ceuca) while the freshest same-surface chain via Grubor leans Mrazikova, so the chains roughly cancel. Both are clay-only players, both played three matches with one three-setter, neither is in doubles, no injury signs found. Bookmakers 1.57/2.20 (about 58% Senica) match Kalshi. I make Senica about 57%: the more proven player at this level, but a coin-flip lean, not a conviction, so no medal.

Gannon (#826, career high, 1.85m right-hander with a big serve, 18 aces in the Dublin final) has the higher ceiling: since June he beat Tomic (#192) at the Dublin Challenger, won M15 Dublin over De Jonge (#568) and Molder (#843), and yesterday beat #493 Boogaard 7-6(2) 6-2 as a 4.31 underdog. rows.analysis: Verified: US Open R3, Grandstand first match Saturday 11am ET (15:00 UTC), not the 18:00 Kalshi placeholder. Books: Keys 1.58-1.67, Zheng 2.35-2.50, so the market already treats #121 Zheng as a top-30 player; the ranking gap is post-surgery noise, not information. H2H 1-1: Keys 7-5 6-1 Washington 2023, Zheng 4-6 6-2 6-4 Miami in March (31 winners to 15 once she adjusted to Keys' pace). Keys is 33-14, R4 at all three 2026 Slams, and won Eastbourne, but her summer hard-court form is wobbly: losses to Samsonova, Kostyuk and Bejlek, then 50 UEs and five match points saved against #73 Bondar in 2h58. Zheng is 11-13 at tour level, 0 wins over top-30 except Keys, and has lost to seven players outside the top 40 this year, but she has won six straight in New York, serves 9-10 aces a match and says she has found her fire. Transitive chains (Ruzic, Siniakova, Gibson) all point to Keys on comparable surfaces; Zheng's sub-50% first-serve rate and 5-6 double faults per match feed Keys' second-serve attack, and Zheng admits she is not fully over an illness. Style cuts the other way: Zheng feeds on pace and beat Keys, Kenin x2, Sakkari and Parks this year while losing to grinders. Net: Keys ~55%, a slight lean under the 60% market price, no medal.

rows.analysis: Verified as US Open WD second round, first match on Stadium 17 at 11am ET Saturday (15:00Z, not Kalshi's 18:00Z); NWS says sunny, no rain. Books are pick'em (1.82/1.81 tennisexplorer, 1.91/1.80 tennisstats) while Kalshi has Routliffe/Sutjiadi at 46-47c, so the pick is also the cheaper side. Routliffe/Sutjiadi have partnered on and off since 2021, won DC in July without dropping a set, went 9-2 on this hard-court swing (losses only to Mihalikova/Nicholls and eventual Cincy champs Bouzkova/Noskova 7-5 7-5) and beat Li/Tauson 6-2 6-2 with one unforced error. rows.analysis: US Open R3, Sat Sep 5, second on Armstrong after the 11:00 ET opener (est. 13:00 ET / 17:00 UTC). Books: Cobolli -110 (1.80-1.85), Blockx +100 (1.92-1.95). Cobolli (#6, RG finalist, Wimbledon QF, Cincinnati SF with wins over Paul #21 and Jodar #13) is the better player and the format helps him: best-of-five dilutes Blockx's serving streaks, and Cobolli is 13-2 at slams this year while Blockx is in his first slam third round. The honest counter: Cobolli has 6h55 on court from two slow-starting matches, calls himself 'slightly more tired', and in 2025 retired in this exact round after long early matches; Blockx is fresher, hit 27 aces in two rounds and was two points from beating him in Cincy. rows.headline: Fresher Bublik serving 80% 1st-serve pts, unbroken here vs Paul in 2025; ~41% vs 39c
rows.analysis: Third-round rematch of the 2025 US Open R3, when Bublik beat Paul in five with 22 aces and was never broken while Paul faded after a set-3 medical timeout. Books have Paul -200 / Bublik +154 (about 61-63% Paul), and Kalshi at 0.61/0.39 matches. Paul is the better 2026 player (38-16, Houston title, Delray/Hamburg/Queen's finals, Cincinnati QF with a match-point save over Zverev), returns far better (38% return pts won vs Bublik's 34%) and is the fitter mover in 85F heat. But Bublik is the fresher man: 1h22m to crush Mannarino 6-3 6-1 6-1 after a four-set win over Wolf, roughly 4h on court versus Paul's 5h45m (2h41m vs Wong, 3h04m vs Prizmic, where Paul won just 48% of second-serve points). Bublik skipped the whole North American swing so his body is rested, and he has won 80% of first-serve points in both rounds. Caveats: Bublik's two wins came against soft opposition (38-year-old Mannarino off a five-setter, Wolf back from shoulder injury), his hard-court level since February was poor (straight-set losses to De Minaur, Auger-Aliassime, Griekspoor, Hijikata, Berrettini), and Paul is 2-1 in ATP main-draw hard meetings. Net: market price is close to fair; I make Bublik ~41% vs the 39c ask, a thin lean on serve-driven variance, no medal.

rows.headline: Home-court W50 finalist vs a seeded veteran who just lost to #589 and #989; price is fair
rows.analysis: Stankovic is the better player on this court right now and the price roughly says so. Last week, as a qualifier at the W50 on these same clay courts, she beat Yamazaki (#647), seeded Granwehr (#317), Milovanovic (#381) and seeded Dencheva (#280) before De Stefano (#250) routed her 0-6 1-6 in the final. Tona's #359 is built on two Mexican W15 finals and a lucky-loser WTA win in Athens; on European clay this year she has beaten nobody ranked above #448 and arrives off losses to Geerlings (#589) and Gniewkowska (#989) in Poland. Stankovic is from Nis, trains at Tennis Academy Zivkovic, and this is her 12th event in Kursumlijska Banja in 2026 (W15 title here in July). The counterweight is load: eight singles plus a doubles in 11 days, a three-tiebreak marathon, the final flop, and a dropped set to an unranked 16-year-old wildcard on Wednesday. Common opponents are thin and roughly cancel (Tona beat lefty Szabo who beat Stankovic; both lost to Maric). Bookmakers sit at 1.56 (~59% de-vigged), Kalshi ask 0.61. I make it about 61%: fair, not cheap. Order of play per Tennis Explorer is 14:00 local (12:00 UTC), not the 17:00 UTC Kalshi lists. No unpriced fact found, so no medal.

rows.title: Radovanovic vs Oz
rows.tournament: W35 Kursumlijska Banja (Serbia) R16, outdoor clay, Tennis Club T Line
rows.headline: Oz is a class above on 2026 results and showed no rust Tuesday; Radovanovic's ceiling stops around #537
rows.analysis: Kalshi's listed 16:00 UTC is wrong: tennisexplorer's order of play has this R16 at 12:30 CEST (10:30 UTC) on Sept 3. Books sit 1.53-1.73 on Oz (consensus ~57%), Kalshi 58c, so the market is fair. Oz (#406, CH 163, 27, 178cm lefty) has real 2026 pedigree on clay: Blois W75 SF beating Riera (#181), Portoroz W50 SF, and two tiebreak sets against #52 Oliynykova at Iasi in July. Concerns are real but partly priced: she retired hurt at 4-6 1-2 against #717 Iliev in Haag qualifying on July 5, then vanished for seven weeks after Iasi (not the Mediterranean Games, no injury news found), skipping the W75/W50 Kursumlijska weeks, and she has lost to #939 Esquiva Banuls and #501 Dittmann on clay this year. Her return, 6-1 6-2 over #448 Sakellaridi on Sept 1, answered the rust question. Radovanovic (#712, 22, righty) is a W15 clay grinder who has practically lived at this venue: 22-7 at Kursumlijska Banja in 2026 with a title and two finals, three blowout wins this week including 6-2 6-0 over #559 Simion. But her ceiling is low: 0-3 against #537 Zaytseva here, losses to Guth (#534), Kotliar (#356), Geerlings, and no 2026 win over anyone better than ~#500. Neither plays doubles this week; both fresh. Oz ~60%, a hair above the ask.

rows.title: Tubello vs Ebeling Koning
rows.tournament: W50 Saint-Palais-sur-Mer (Open 17) R16, outdoor clay, Tennis Club Saint-Palaisien, France
rows.headline: Clay class gap: #222 defending champ at home vs #475 qualifier on a 29-match summer grind
rows.analysis: Tubello (25, FRA, #222, CH #198 in Jul) is a clay specialist: 9 of her 10 ITF titles on clay, 22-5 on clay in 2025, and in 2026 she won San Gregorio twice and Bujumbura W50, made the Istanbul 125 SF (beat P. Kudermetova), the Vaihingen final and the Contrexeville 125 QF. She won this exact event last year (beat Avdeeva in the final) and is seeded 3. Ebeling Koning (20, NED, #475 = career high) is on a genuine surge, 24-5 since Jul 5 with W75 Koksijde and W50 Oldenzaal semis, and beat #393 Kovackova 6-3 6-3 yesterday as a 2.28 dog, but her losses in that run came to exactly the tier Tubello sits above (Basiletti #267, Schunk #315, both in straights) and she is 1-2 vs top-320 in 2026. The negatives on Tubello are real and visible: she retired at Roehampton on Aug 6 while up a set, has two hip surgeries in her history, then lost a three-setter to #156 Hon at US Open qualifying and needed a 7-6(8) first set vs #776 Iliev yesterday. That is why the books sit at 1.63-1.67 (fair ~56%) rather than the 1.40 the ranking gap implies, and Kalshi at 0.57 matches them. Ebeling Koning also played a SF in the Netherlands on Aug 29 then qualifying in western France on Aug 31. Weather is morning fog clearing to sun, 26C, moderate wind: slow, heavy clay early, which suits the grinder. Net: Tubello ~60%, a small lean over the ask, no unpriced fact.

rows.title: Rispoli vs Batin
rows.tournament: ITF M15 Buzau (ROU) quarterfinal, outdoor clay
rows.headline: Rispoli lost 12 games in 4 rounds and crushed #850 Tenti 6-2 6-1 on this court
rows.analysis: First meeting. Market (Kalshi 46/54, book 1.99/1.71) leans Batin on rank (#1009 vs #1572), home soil and freshness - fair, but it under-rates Rispoli's week. The Italian qualifier has won 48 games and lost 12 in four matches, beating Ignatik (#1300, ex-#129) 6-3 6-2 and, crucially, Fermin Tenti (#850, CH #561, in Challenger-qualifying form) 6-2 6-1 on this same clay yesterday - a man 160 spots ABOVE Batin. Batin's best scalp, Gima (#589), is a lefty who has lost to M15 Romanians all year, so that #589 is playing like a #900. Chains lean Rispoli: Andreescu (#594) beat Tenti by the same margin Rispoli did and handled Batin 6-3 6-1; Ignatik beat Cazacu, who beat Batin. Batin's floor is low - 1-6 1-6 to unranked Ghetu, 3-6 3-6 to Madaras a week ago. Against that, Rispoli plays his 5th match in 5 days at 29 in ~30C, is 2-7 in 2026 main draws and has never cracked #1329, so regression is live. Net: a genuine coin flip nudged Rispoli's way, and 0.49 is the better price than 0.56.

rows.analysis: W15 Pecs, outdoor clay, R16. Kalshi (0.59) sits on top of the book (1.58/2.21 = 58.3% devigged), so there is no pricing gap - this is a fundamentals call. Stevic, #1093, is in dismal form: 6-15 in W15 main draws in 2026, blown out 2-6 2-6 by #1071 Sagmar on Aug 26, and three mid-match retirements since Jun 2025. But Biro is worse where it counts. She is unranked in WTA singles and 1-3 in W15 main draws this year, that lone win a Tkachenko retirement at 6-0 4-0 - zero completed main-draw wins in 2026. Every 2026 meeting with a ranked opponent was a rout: 0-6 2-6 (Drobysheva), 1-6 1-6 (Anikina), 3-6 0-6 (Rasim), 5-7 2-6 (Artemeva), 6-7 6-2 0-10 to #936 Goina. The one clean chain favours Stevic: she beat #739 Artemeva 6-0 7-5 on clay as a 1.46 favourite, the same Artemeva who beat Biro 7-5 6-2. It is 13 months stale and Stevic has declined since, so this is a lean, not a medal. Biro's home court, youth, three-match streak and lighter Sep 2 (27 games vs Stevic's 46 across singles+doubles) keep it close.

rows.analysis: W15 Fiano Romano R16, red clay, 11:30 local. Ormaechea's #1226 badly understates her: ex-world #59, 389-220 lifetime on clay, 12-5 on clay in 2026 including qualifying into the $30k Trieste and reaching the QF, losing only to champion Ce. Two days ago she beat 3rd seed Gennaro (#918) 6-4 6-2 as a 2.43 underdog on these exact courts. Sevcikova (#947, CH #708) is 20-18 in 2026, but 8 wins came at a non-ITF Czech UTR series; her sanctioned record is ~12-14 and clay is 9-9. She has beaten nobody inside the top ~700 all year and is blown out at that tier: 2-6 1-6 Barbulescu (#690), 0-6 2-6 Safta, 1-6 1-6 Vogt, 1-6 2-6 Zucchini. Ormaechea beat that same Barbulescu, the [2] seed, 1-6 6-3 7-5 on clay in July. Sevcikova self-describes as a serve-and-forehand aggressor with chronic back trouble; slow Italian clay versus a career Argentine clay grinder is the wrong matchup, and she needed three sets to beat #1448 qualifier Valente. Books: Ormaechea 1.58 / Sevcikova 2.24 (58.6% vig-free). I make Ormaechea ~65%.

Books have Lahey 58.9% de-vigged (2.25/1.57); the schedule collision nudges me just past that.

rows.headline: Market over-taxes one Q-round loss; Milovanovic clearly better on these courts
rows.analysis: W35 Kursumlijska Banja R16, outdoor clay, 11:00 local. Cakarevic owns the H2H 2-0 (6-0 6-1 at this venue May 2024; 6-2 6-1 in W100 Maspalomas qualifying Jul 27) - 26 games to 4, which is exactly why an unseeded #578 is priced at 48% against the #7 seed. But the 2024 match came when Cakarevic was ~150 spots the better player, so the live evidence is one qualifying match five weeks ago, played after Milovanovic had sat idle 18 days. Since Aug 9 both have contested the SAME four events on the SAME courts: Milovanovic 7-3 - qualified at a W75, beat #291 Kaji at a W50, lost two tiebreaks to the eventual finalist; Cakarevic 3-3, crushed 1-6 1-6 by #640 Golovina, wins only over qualifying-level opposition. The Kuzmova (#278) chain also favours Milovanovic. Offsetting: Milovanovic played the last match of the day (17:45 start, 6-3 1-6 6-3 over #1434 Virc) and returns at 11:00; Cakarevic won in ~62 minutes from 12:50. Dry, 29C, no rain. Thin lean, nothing the price has plainly missed.

rows.analysis: Books have this 1.84/1.84 -- a true coin flip -- because Cvetkovic's maiden W35 title (Verbier, Aug 30, beating Okutoyi #488 and Strakhova #525) is fully visible against Martinez Cirez's four straight 1R exits. Martinez Cirez has played twice in 15 days and skipped doubles. Common opponents lean Spain too. Cvetkovic is the better trajectory and is home; Martinez Cirez is the better player in these specific conditions with fresher legs.

Chan has 21 WTA doubles titles (CH #5); Joint (dbl #30) won Monterrey on Aug 29 and upset Samsonova in the US Open R1. The Williams side is a wildcard reunion with one match together in four years - a 2-6 6-1 [8-10] loss to Kostyuk/Stearns. Serena skipped US Open singles because the knee wasn't right. Crucially the 'two points away' Cincy story happened under no-ad plus a match tiebreak; a slam is ad scoring and a full third set in 86F storms. The read that moves me is surface: TennisExplorer's 2026 splits show Knaff 14-10 INDOORS but just 2-2 on outdoor hard — his whole 2026 credential (M15 Oslo final, Lugano quali wins over Arnaboldi/Forti, Davis Cup, Cherbourg) is indoor. Second, Dalmasso's ugly L-L-L-L-L run before today was entirely Challenger-level: Mayo #362, Trotter #406, Matsuoka (CH #309), Barroso Campos #531 (on grass), Johns — all far above Knaff's level. At his own level he won M15 Vaasa in June (d. Peliwo 6-4 7-5) and beat Dando 5-7 6-4 6-3 today. Third, Knaff has completed ONE competitive singles match since May 7 (a July loss); today's 6-1 was a retirement, so he arrives rusty. Against me: both common opponents favor Knaff — but both came indoors in his Jan-Mar peak. Knaff is also fresher. I make it ~60%.

rows.title: Tan vs Johnson
rows.tournament: ITF W50 Leiria (Portugal) R1, outdoor hard
rows.headline: Tan a class above at W50 level and a 2025 Leiria semifinalist; Johnson has beaten nobody inside #300
rows.analysis: Books sit at Tan 1.49-1.53 / Johnson 2.37-2.63 (Pinnacle 1.53/2.53, moved toward Tan from a 1.60 open), i.e. ~62% Tan. Tan (#216, CH #90) is the seed with the far better resume: W50 Croissy-Beaubourg title in March, RG/Wimbledon Q3R, Ilkley QF, and in July at the WTA125 Istanbul she beat Havlickova and Gasanova (#192) before retiring 1-6 0-1 down to Vandewinkel (~#100). She reached the Leiria SF on these courts a year ago. The knock is fitness and rust: the unexplained Istanbul retirement, a Prague withdrawal, then a single match in six weeks (6-4 6-3 loss to Stoiana, #122, who went on to qualify). Johnson (#459, 22, 6ft, ex-Old Dominion All-American) is match-sharp after two qualifying wins and a doubles win here, but her 2026 record is two W15 titles and a string of R1/R2 losses at W35+ level to Dolehide (#260), Hunter (~#190), Kaji (~#290), Liutova (twice), Arango, Rogers and T. Pieri; she has no win over a top-300 player. Shared opponents lean Tan (Tan 6-0 6-3 over Rogers; Johnson 1-1 with her). Cool, gusty conditions (21mph gusts, 20C) favor Tan's slice-and-variety game over a tall ball-striker. Fair ~64% Tan, but the Kalshi ask of 0.81 is well above fair on a $110-volume market, so size small. No medal: the retirement, layoff and Johnson's ledger are all on public results pages and already in the 1.50 price.

Rublev (#24) survived LL Virtanen (#109) from two sets down in 3h42 on Monday, saving a match point, converting 7/24 break points with 27 UEs; he did serve superbly (20 aces, 82% first-serve points, 92% holds). Matsuda (#483, 183cm, serve-first) owns the better season: three Futures titles since Jul 2025 and Challenger QFs at Samsun and Istanbul in Jul-Aug, and books opened him 1.57. But he has played ~654 points on three straight days in 30C/88% humidity: 267 points vs doubles specialist Uesugi (#1394 singles), broken three times by Meng (#1027), then 7-6 7-6 over Delaney (#365) converting 1 of 11 break points. His return won only 8-24% of return games this week and his second serve 32-55%. Leong (#551, 22) has played ~280 points: 6-0 ret, 6-1 6-4 over Palan (#506), then 7-6(3) 6-3 over lefty 8th seed Bar Biryukov (#288) while saving 7/8 break points and converting 3/4. Common opponents split (Leong better vs Takahashi/Dev/Shin, Matsuda better vs Samrej/Santillan/Sinclair), no H2H, though they were doubles partners at Bali M25 in Sep 2025 so nothing is a surprise. The line has already moved to 1.84/1.86 (Betfair 1.82/1.99), so the freshness gap is mostly priced; I make Leong ~54% on fatigue plus serve-hold form. Rain is forecast and a push to Thursday would reset Matsuda's legs.

rows.title: Trotter vs Hsu
rows.tournament: International Challenger Zhangjiagang (CH75, China) R16, outdoor hard
rows.headline: Hsu is the real Challenger player here; Trotter is 1-9 vs top-350 foes in 2026 and lost the last H2H at his peak
rows.analysis: Zhangjiagang R16, first match on Court 6 at 11:00 local (03:00 UTC, not Kalshi's 06:00). Books have Hsu 1.56-1.58 / Trotter 2.2-2.32 (fair ~59% Hsu); Kalshi asks 0.63. Hsu (#268, CH 158) is a steady Challenger QF-level player: Winnipeg QF in July losing only to eventual champion Samuel (#110), an M25 Taipei title in August beating Dellavedova (#293), then R1 here 7-6(4) 5-5 when Ymer (#204) collapsed in the heat. Trotter (#464, CH 170) has cratered in 2026: he retired at Gwangju qualifying in April, missed seven weeks, lost two Futures matches in June, went 0-3 in Canadian Challenger main draws (Chidekh 6-1 6-2, Draxl, Zink), then sat out all of August before beating wildcard Cui (#454) 6-3 6-4 as a pick'em. His only 2026 win over anyone inside #350 is Matsuoka (#250) in Vancouver qualifying. H2H is 1-1, but Hsu's 6-3 6-3 Busan win came in Apr 2025 with Trotter at his career-high; Trotter's Yokkaichi 2023 win was on faster Japanese hard. Transitive chain via Moriya (Hsu won 6-2 6-3, Trotter lost) leans Hsu. Trotter has one extra rest day and a live serve (10 aces vs Cui), and Hsu has had bad losses (Gorzny #876, Mmoh), so 65% is the ceiling. No unpriced factor found: everything here is on public result pages, so no medal.

rows.title: Forti vs Clarke
rows.tournament: Como Lake Challenger R32 (Challenger 75), Como, Italy, outdoor clay
rows.headline: Clarke's class, clay pedigree and H2H win at a coin-flip price books make 52/48
rows.analysis: Official OOP: 3rd on Court 1 from 10:00 CEST (~11:30 UTC est). Books price Clarke 1.77 v Forti 1.92 (~52% no-vig); Kalshi is 50/50. The retail read — home Italian clay grinder v traveling Brit — inverts under research: clay is Clarke's BEST surface (189-102 career, 3 M25 clay titles in 2024, two at Santa Margherita di Pula), and he beat Forti 7-6(3) 6-3 on that same Italian Futures circuit in May 2023 when Forti was near his career-high level. Clarke's ugly 20-26 season is losses to top-200 players (Sakamoto #157 who then beat Muller, Chidekh #176, Kym #186 — all 3-setters); v #300+ opposition he mostly wins, and Forti is #363. Forti's comeback from a foot double bone oedema (#600 in March to #363) is real but Futures-padded (~8-9 Challenger MD wins); his last meeting with a Clarke-ranked opponent ended 6-1 6-3 to Cecchinato (#195) three weeks ago, and he retired from a Futures match Aug 18 before playing quali here. Forti's court time in Como and home crowd keep this close, but at equal 50c I side with the sharper book lean, class and H2H. Clarke ~53%.

Both come in rested (~3-4 weeks idle); Kulikova's 29-day layoff plus US-to-China travel is the main drag on her, Yao has been home since mid-August. Chains and current level favor Kulikova modestly; home comfort, surface base and H2H favor Yao. I make it a slight Kulikova lean at 53% vs a 49c ask.

Style backs it: BB is a 196cm lefty, Leong 175cm right-handed, and Leong's season losses cluster against bigger hitters (Castelnuovo x2, Skatov, Shin 6-2 6-2). The market has already discounted BB hard (1.53-1.56, ~59%) for a poor month: 1R M15 loss to unranked Qian Sun 6-3 6-4 on Aug 26, a 6-4 6-2 Challenger loss to Cui Jie, a mid-match retirement Aug 4. That discount looks a touch too large: a #286 with a 2-0 same-surface H2H over a #551 qualifier should sit nearer 63-65%. Transitive chains are genuinely even (both lost 3-setters to Simakin, both beat Huang Tsung-Hao). Leong is sharper and heat-adapted (32C, humid) but plays a third straight day and his qualy wins came over #496 Palan plus a retirement.

transitive.summary: Only two shared opponents and both cancel: each lost a first-set-up three-setter to Simakin, each beat Huang Tsung-Hao in straights. Chains are too thin to move the number; the direct H2H carries it.

rows.analysis: Barki is really a doubles player (doubles CH #447, singles CH #1344, now #1921) with just three completed singles matches since July 2025. He returned from a wrist layoff at UTR PTT Bali on Aug 17, beat Thomas Patton 6-4 7-5, then withdrew from his next match on Aug 18 when the wrist flared again (Sofascore logs a walkover; antaranews and viva name the injury). He is a home wildcard here and also plays doubles R16 with Ellis the same day. Perez Ramos is #953, at a career high set Aug 3, 21-6 in singles in 2026 all on hard with two Futures finals and a SF, and he beat Shanker Heisnam - the #3 seed in this event's qualifying - 6-2 6-4 in May. He is ruthless against sub-level fields (6-0 6-3, 6-1 6-0, 6-3 6-3). Against that, he has not played since a flat Aug 4 loss to Coquelin at M25 Roehampton and must arrive into Nusa Dua heat and humidity from Europe, while Barki is acclimatised and has played this venue repeatedly. Rust and a home crowd are the genuine counterweights and ITF first rounds are chaotic, but the level gap plus a wrist that failed 14 days ago is the bigger fact. No bookmaker has priced this match at all.

rows.analysis: M25 Urayasu (SBC Dream Tennis, $30k outdoor hard, Chiba), R32, Sept 1. Lee is the 6th seed, #616, 17-16 in 2026 and runner-up at M25 Ma'anshan in April (l. Alastair Gray 2-6 3-6) — a genuine M25-level player. Katayama is a 37-year-old home wildcard, #1523, 170cm, Japan's domestic #41; TennisExplorer lists ZERO singles matches for him in 2026 and his last singles match was Matsuyama Challenger in Nov 2025. He entered three ITF events in Jun–Jul 2026 in doubles only; his last match of any kind was doubles on 8 Jul. That layoff, at 37, in Tokyo heat over best-of-three, is the biggest fact here. Against it: Lee retired hurt at 3-6 1-1 vs Shiraishi (#488) on 26 Aug and has retired 3-4 times in 2026 — but Taiwanese press confirms he then played doubles at the same event to the semi-finals, so the injury reads managed, not disabling. He also lost the only H2H (2017 Futures final). Taipei→Tokyo travel after a typhoon-compressed week is a real but small drag. Common opponents (Ochi, Hazawa) lean Lee. Lee ~70% — but at a 90c ask this is not a buy.

rows.headline: Gea's 2026 hard-court resume beats a clay-built lefty who is 1-3 in hard slam main draws
rows.analysis: First meeting, priced as a coin flip and it nearly is. Cerundolo (#45) is 42 spots higher but his ranking is clay-built: Bordeaux Challenger title, RG R16 off a cramping Sinner, and just 1-3 lifetime in hard-court slam main draws. On hard in 2026 he is 7-5, best win Rinderknech in two tiebreaks, and he was blown out by Ruud (1-6 2-6) and Auger-Aliassime (5-7 1-6). Gea is ~13-3 on hard in 2026 with wins over Lehecka (best-of-5 at the AO), Francisco Cerundolo and Shapovalov en route to the Los Cabos title, is 31-12 on hard vs 14-14 on clay at CH/ITF level, and is 2-1 vs lefties on hard this year. Against it: Gea played zero matches Aug 1-23, then lost the final qualifying round 3-6 1-6 to #156 Basavareddy on these courts serving badly, and best-of-5 in mid-80s humidity is the grinder's arena — Cerundolo has 8 tour hard matches in 17 days and elite stamina. rows.analysis: Porto Open qualifying final, outdoor clay. Schoen is the better player on paper: 37-11 in 2026 with two M15 Kayseri titles and an M25 Figueira da Foz final.
