Fuele has played 30 of 30 matches in 2026 on clay (125-79 career) and six weeks ago qualified into the Cordenons Ch75 semis, beating top seed Hugo Dellien and Thiago Seyboth Wild. The counterweight is real: Fuele retired at M15 Xativa on Jul 30, lost 5-7 0-6 to #1043 Gavrielides at Augsburg on Aug 23, and needed 2h+ over three sets yesterday while Schoen spent 65 minutes. rows.headline: Kamput beat the #4 seed; that seed was 2 rounds better than Choudhary in May
rows.analysis: Final qualifying round at M15 Nonthaburi 04, outdoor hard. Both men are effectively unranked: Kamput is a 17-y-o Thai wildcard (ITF junior #899, no men's ranking); Choudhary is 24, ITF-unranked, career high #1913. The flat 1.85/1.84 is a default price with no information in it. What it misses: Kamput's Q1 win was over the [4] seed Tanakorn Srirat (ATP #1735) 6-3 6-3, and Srirat reached the QF of M15 Nakhon Pathom 03 in May - the same Thai hard-court event where Choudhary lost his opening main-draw match 0-6 0-6 to Chanta (#844). Srirat's career best (#1705) also tops Choudhary's (#1913). Choudhary beat only the [16] seed, an unranked Indian. Kamput was the sole winner among six Thai wildcards (others lost 0-6 0-6, 1-6 0-6, 2-6 3-6, 2-6 3-6) and arrives 11-1 across two J30 weeks at this same club, so he is match-tight and acclimatised to the 31C humidity. Against that: Choudhary has far more pro experience, has qualified into M15 main draws before, handles Thai M15 opposition (beat seeds [6] and [14] in May), and Kamput's only other pro match was a 0-6 0-6 loss at M25 level in April.

rows.analysis: The market prices Gueymard ~58% (1.61/2.19) off a 332-vs-491 gap, but both numbers are stale. Gueymard's 332 is propped up by January indoor points (Quimper SF); since June he is 5-7, is 1-3 on outdoor hard in 2026, and has not hit a competitive ball since 28 Jul — no ITF, no exhibition, not even on the Augsburg entry list. This is a first match back after five weeks, at 32-33C, on his weakest surface, in a qualifying draw he'd have skipped a year ago. Almazan's 491 lags badly: he was 858 in January, gained 57 places from Pozoblanco alone, and on outdoor hard at Challenger level in 2026 he is 9-3, including 7-6(4) 6-2 over 8th seed Alastair Gray (#282) and a three-set loss to Santillan (~#301). He is 6-0 in hard-court Challenger qualifying this year; Gueymard is 1-2. Add the home wildcard: Mallorcan, Palma-based, no travel, heat-acclimatised. Gueymard still owns the bigger weapons, an R16 on these exact courts in 2025 and a 7-6(4) 6-3 win over #152 Budkov Kjaer on 21 Jul, so this is close — but 43c is too cheap.

rows.tournament: Como Lake Challenger (CH75) final qualifying round, outdoor red clay, Tennis Como
rows.headline: Nikles a level up - M25 finalist vs an M15 QF loser - and won the July clay meeting
rows.analysis: Qualifying final at Como (outdoor red clay, Tennis Como); winner enters the main draw. Nikles (#424, CH #256) is a genuine M25/Challenger clay grinder: M25 Castelldefels final in April, Mataro SF in May, Bucaramanga Challenger QF, 5-2 at CH75 level in 2026, 272-172 career on clay. Rottoli (#901, CH #403 back in 2023) has slid to M15 level - he lost the M15 Vienna QF 3-6 3-6 on Aug 28 and is 14-16 this year. But they met eight weeks ago on Moroccan clay at M25 Rabat and Nikles needed 6-7(3) 7-5 7-5, so the on-court gap is smaller than the rankings, which is why the price sits at 62c not 75c. Tiebreakers for Nikles: he beat Kasra Rahmani (#778) 6-2 6-4 on this exact court yesterday, and Rahmani beat Rottoli 6-4 6-2 on clay in April; and Rottoli played three matches in Vienna Aug 26-28, moved ~700km, then came from 1-4 down to edge La Vela. Offsetting: Rottoli was born in Como, this is his home event, and Nikles is 2-4 in his last six official matches. Fair near 67% - a thin edge on the 63c ask, not a medal.

rows.headline: Rankings dead level, Tabacco owns the H2H and is the higher seed - 41c is too cheap
rows.analysis: Plovdiv 3 (Challenger 50, outdoor clay), final qualifying round. Rankings are effectively tied - Tabacco ~#650, Kirkin ~#657 - and Tabacco is seeded [6] to Kirkin's [7], so the entry list itself rates this a coin flip. Kirkin's case is level: he is 5-2 in final qualifying rounds in 2026 (qualified at Soma Bay, Split, Shymkent, Grodzisk, Hamburg), beat Zeballos 6-3 6-3, and took a set off ex-#40 Ivashka; career high #251 vs #599. That is real and it is why he is favoured. But Tabacco won their only meeting (6-3 3-6 6-3, Feb 2024), beat Ouakaa 6-4 6-3 at M15 Monastir in April where Kirkin lost to that same man 6-4 6-3 in the June final at the same venue, and beat Naw, who beat Kirkin in July. Tabacco also came through Q1 far more cleanly (6-2 6-1 over Shandarov vs Kirkin's 6-4 6-2) and is a clay-raised Italian at 20-14 on dirt this year. Bookmakers price Tabacco 2.11 / Kirkin 1.56 - de-vigged 42.5%, above Kalshi's 41c ask. I make it ~45%: Kirkin is the better player, but not by 19 points.

rows.title: Nedic vs Lokoli
rows.tournament: Como Lake Challenger (CH75), final qualifying round, outdoor red clay, Como ITA
rows.headline: Lokoli's hot streak is all M25; vs top-250 opposition he's been beaten all year
rows.analysis: Q-final round, top quali seed (Nedic, #252) vs #8 seed (Lokoli, #434), red clay. Both won R1 easily Sunday — Nedic 6-0 6-0 over 17yo wildcard Garbero (CH #1340), Lokoli 6-2 6-1 over Angelini (CH #593), so Lokoli's win was the better one. Lokoli is genuinely scorching: M25 titles at Ajaccio (Jul 5), Bastia-Lucciana (Jul 12, no set lost) and Lesa (Aug 23, 50km from Como), plus 5-1 in Tennis-Bundesliga on clay incl. wins over Santillan/Sachko and an 11-9 champions-TB loss to Monteiro. But the level gap is the whole story: against players in Nedic's band (~#150-300) Lokoli lost all year — Gueymard Wayenburg 1-6 2-6, Gojo 3-6 3-6, Giustino 3-6 4-6, Feldbausch 2-6 4-6, Kasnikowski, Chidekh, Brancaccio. Nedic beat Mayot 6-2 6-0 and Nagal 6-1 7-6(2), made the Istanbul CH75 final, and is 30-20 on clay. He's slumping (5-8 since Jul, lost from a set up to #339 Estevez on Aug 24) and that plus Lokoli's form is exactly why this is 59c not 68c. Fair, slight lean Nedic. 31 vs 21 in 28C heat helps too.

transitive.summary: Chains cancel: both beat Kirkin in 3 and Karol in 2, both lost to Gueymard Wayenburg and Monteiro. Lokoli's Monteiro match was closer but a Bundesliga match-tiebreak; Nedic's GW loss was tighter. Too thin to move the number.

rows.analysis: Manacor qualifying R1, outdoor hard, ~32C. Gengel #390 (131pts) vs Hernandez Serrano #471 (99pts); first meeting. 2026 records diverge sharply: Gengel 34-13 with two ITF titles and a January Challenger final at Nonthaburi on hard, beating Luka Pavlovic (#217) 6-2 6-2 and Kolar 6-2 7-5. Hernandez is 17-20, one win in his last six, four straight singles losses (1-6 4-6 Saraiva, 4-6 4-6 Hurrion, 1-6 0-6 Tomic). Hard is Gengel's surface (17 ITF titles, mostly hard) and at 1.85m he outserves the 1.75m Mexican. Two chains agree: both lost to J.B. Torres on clay this season, Gengel 4-6 6-3 6-3 on Aug 17, Hernandez 6-2 6-0 in June; and Gengel beat Hurrion 6-1 7-6(5) where Hernandez lost. Hernandez also flew Kingston (Aug 25 loss) to Mallorca, seven zones east, for a morning start. Against that: Gengel is idle since Aug 17, has ~3 competitive singles matches since June, last played on clay, and slid from Manacor's main draw in 2025 to qualifying now. Fair ~62 vs a 58 ask - a lean, not a mispricing.

rows.title: Lee vs Sidorova
rows.tournament: ITF W15 Tianjin (5th of series), Tianjin International Tennis Center, final qualifying round, outdoor hard
rows.headline: Higher-ranked, in-rhythm Lee is worth more than the 40c ask; 62c on Sidorova is rich
rows.analysis: Deciding qualifying round, W15 Tianjin, outdoor hard, ~33C, 10:00 local. Rankings favour Lee: #345 vs #401, Q-seed 2 vs 10. Lee is sharp and acclimatised - second straight week at this venue, 6-1 6-2 over Yuan (Q-seed 14) and 6-1 6-2 over Chanta (#460), then a comeback 2-6 6-4 6-1 over Ayano Shimizu (#401, CH #175) on this court yesterday. Sidorova is the better talent on paper - 2025 W15 title, Maanshan final in March, scalps of Lansere (#265) and Kaji at WTA level - and the transitive chains lean her way. She is also far fresher: one 55-minute win in a fortnight against Lee's five matches in six days including two three-setters. Offsetting that, Sidorova has played only three matches since 18 June and lost her last completed one, on Serbian clay, then flew to China. Book (2.23/1.58 = 41/59 normalised) and Kalshi (~39/61) both price Sidorova 58-60%. I make it about 56/44. That leaves Lee thin value at the 0.40 ask and Sidorova clearly overpriced at 0.62. This is a price call, not a conviction call.

transitive.summary: Chains lean Sidorova - she beat Lansere the day after Lansere beat Lee at the same event, and owns a Kaji win Lee has no answer to. But all of it is 5-12 months old; the fresh Chanta chain goes Lee's way.

rows.analysis: W75 Tianjin final qualifying round, outdoor hard, ~33C, 10am local. No H2H at any level. Adkar (#390) is higher ranked but her form is soft: the W15 Tianjin SF run came over three qualifiers (Shimizu 6-0 6-0, Lee Eunji 6-2 6-0, #741 Plipuech in three sets), and the one ranked player she met, champion Shi Han (#262), bagelled her 1-6 0-6 on Aug 29. She is 0-5 since April versus opponents inside roughly the top 300, and Monday is her 6th match in 6 days. Huang (#477) has one match in 14 days and won it over the No.9 seed, ex-#114 Wei Sijia, 6-4 6-4. Her ceiling is fresher: W100 Wuning final in June as a qualifier, beating Shi Han 6-2 6-2 on Chinese hard, plus Nugroho, who had beaten Adkar in BJK Cup. Caveats: Shi Han was mid-slump in June and is flying now, Huang's last two events (clay, Serbia) were poor, and Adkar is heat-adapted, match-sharp and knows these courts. Four books at ~1.71/2.01 have Huang 54%; I have her a shade higher, so this is a thin lean, not a mispricing.

Both had soft Sunday openers: Palan 6-4 6-3 over 32-y-o doubles specialist JiSung Nam (alternate, doubles #143), Leong 6-0 when WC Weiyi Kong retired after one set. rows.analysis: W35 Verbier 2 final, outdoor synthetic clay at 1480m. Okutoyi (#503, CH #414) is 17-6 in 2026 with two W35 Nairobi titles on murram clay at ~1700m - Verbier is the closest thing on tour to her home conditions. Her run here is the better one: she beat top seed Ryser (#261, two 2026 titles) 6-7 6-0 7-6, and Grammatikopoulou 6-2 6-3 - and Grammatikopoulou had just WON Verbier 1 on these same courts, beating Cvetkovic 6-2 7-6 in that semifinal. Cvetkovic (#920, CH #835) is a real talent - ITF junior #8, Roland Garros girls QF - and her ranking understates her, but her pro record outside this fortnight is 4-4 with repeated first-round exits, and her best win here is Strakhova (#525). Workload also inverts the obvious read: Cvetkovic has played 9 matches in 11 days including qualifying and four 3-setters; Okutoyi 7, one ending in retirement. The counter is real - Okutoyi spent ~3 hours on court today while Cvetkovic won 6-4 6-4, and an 18-year-old in her first pro final is dangerous. At 50/50 with negligible volume ($43 on the Cvetkovic side), Okutoyi at 51c is the value.

rows.headline: Lefty owns this matchup: 5-0 H2H all on hard, and hard-Elo is #38 vs #79
rows.analysis: Hard-court Elo (Tennis Abstract, Aug 24) is the cleanest read: Shapovalov 1773 (#38 hard) vs Kecmanovic 1703 (#79 hard), a 70-pt gap worth ~60% in Bo3 and ~62-63% over five sets, where the favourite's edge compounds. Add a 5-0 official H2H (6-0 with a 2016 Futures), every meeting on hard, the last three all deciding-set wins for the lefty. Venue: Shapovalov is 14-5 lifetime at Flushing with a 2020 QF and R3s in 2023 and 2025; Kecmanovic has never reached R3 in seven visits and lost R1 to Fonseca last year. Style: Kecmanovic went 1-3 vs big lefty servers on hard in 2026 (lost Shelton, lost Tien, beat Atmane), all tight. Recent wins favour Shapo too - Norrie #33 and Mannarino #67 vs Kecmanovic's Ugo Carabelli #76 and Shimabukuro #87, and Kec lost in straights to Marozsan (#63, his own level) four days ago. The offset is real and is why books sit at 55 not 62: Shapovalov retired three times in 2026, fractured a rib at Queen's and sprained the ankle in the Los Cabos final. But he beat Mannarino 6-1 6-4 nine days after that retirement, went the distance with Jodar, and practised with Djokovic on Armstrong Thursday. 58% - a lean, not an edge.

rows.tournament: US Open R1, Flushing Meadows, outdoor hard (best-of-5)
rows.headline: Buse beat a #51-#93 field on these exact courts; Giron lost R1 there to a #394
rows.analysis: Buse (#34) is the better player right now and proved it on these exact courts: at Winston-Salem he beat Walton (#93), Altmaier (#65), J.M. Cerundolo (#51) and Bonzi to reach the final, while Giron (#77) lost round one there in about an hour to lucky loser Dhakshineswar Suresh (#394). That caps a wretched hard swing for Giron, also beaten by 17-year-old Cruz Hewitt (#612) in Washington and Rocha (#125) in Cincinnati qualifying, with no ATP hard main-draw win since Indian Wells in March. Buse won their only meeting 3-6 7-5 7-6(8) at Queen's, though Giron held three match points. The counterweight is workload: Buse has played five straight days (Aug 25-29) including today's final, then travels to New York for best-of-five. But Flashscore, OddsPortal and the Peruvian press all put this match on Aug 31 or Sept 1, not Aug 30, so he gets one or two full rest days, and at 22 he recovers better than a fading 33-year-old. Kalshi (52.5c) and the books (Buse 1.83 / Giron 1.96, ~51.7% devigged) agree; I make it 56%. Thin edge, no mispricing to point at.

rows.analysis: Books split this 1.96/1.99 and Kalshi echoes it, but the last eight weeks are one-directional. Cincinnati is the cleanest read: Faria eased past Wu 6-3 7-5 in qualifying on Aug 13, then five days later on the same courts, after beating Brooksby and Shelton, needed 4-6 6-4 7-6(3) to get by Walton. Same event, same surface, same week. Walton was in that main draw on merit and beat Buse 6-4 6-3 there; Buse went on to the Winston-Salem final. Wu could not clear qualifying. At Newport (Ch125, grass) both were seeded top five: Walton made the final with six championship points, beating McDonald 6-1 6-3 and Michelsen 7-6(2) 6-4; Wu lost R1 to Kozlov, #296. Walton also beat Diallo on hard in February where Wu lost to him in Miami. The counter-case is real but stale: Wu's Acapulco QF run (d. Ruud, Hijikata, Shimabukuro) was February, and both Hijikata and Shimabukuro beat Walton that same month. Wu is fresher, one match in 17 days against Walton's five, and has the higher ceiling. But best-of-five rewards the match-hardened body, and Walton has 63 matches and a five-set win over Medvedev this year.

The driver is Sakamoto's qualifying run, but the headline scalp, Nishikori, is a 36-year-old wildcard ranked #464 in his farewell year; the only real win was Muller (#138) 6-3 6-3, and Q1 vs Clarke (#239) went three. Vukic beat Sakamoto 6-4 7-6(5) on hard in Tokyo qualifying last September, and his 2026 hard scalps are better: Svajda (#80) 6-3 6-1 at an ATP 500, Jacquet (#107) 7-6 6-1, Tsitsipas 7-6 7-6, a Granby Challenger title, a set off Musetti. Against that, the fresh chain favours Sakamoto - same week at Quebec he pushed champion Van Assche (#40) to a third-set breaker while Vukic lost straights to finalist Sakellaridis (#136) - and Vukic is 0-3 lifetime in US Open main draws, 6-17 at slams, 30 and sliding. Sakamoto's 1.93m serve (19 aces, 91% holds) is the profile that beat Vukic twice via Virtanen this year. Genuinely close; I make it ~53/47, so 41c on Vukic is the value side, not a strong opinion.

rows.title: Parry vs Mertens
rows.tournament: Monterrey Open (Abierto GNP Seguros) WTA 500 Final, outdoor hard, Club Sonoma
rows.headline: Parry beat Mertens on hard 14 days ago and has 4 top-50 scalps this week; 37c is short
rows.analysis: Monterrey WTA 500 final, outdoor hard at Club Sonoma, ~95F day cooling into an evening start, no rain risk. The market is a pure ranking/experience line: Mertens #24, 10 titles, 10-6 in finals, versus Parry #50 in her first ever tour-level final (she was 0-6 in prior WTA semis). The tennis says otherwise. Parry beat Mertens 2-6 6-2 6-2 on outdoor hard in Cincinnati 14 days ago, taking the last two sets 12-4 as her slice, one-handed backhand and drop shots dragged a rhythm counterpuncher out of shape. Parry is 8-1 in her last nine; this week she has beaten Vekic #36, Oliynykova #46, Tauson #42 and Li #30 — four top-50 players. Mertens' run is Udvardy #76 (3 sets, 1h56), Starodubtseva #74 and Bartunkova #38 (3 sets, 2h17 from 6-1 3-0 down), and she arrived having lost 1-6 2-6 to Osaka and then to Parry. Mertens is fresher by a match (bye) with ~2h less court time, but plays a fourth straight day at 30; Parry had Wednesday off. Fair looks near 55/45 Mertens, so 37c on Parry is short. No hidden fact here — just a price leaning too hard on rank.

rows.analysis: Bookies (Svrcina 1.92 / Royer 1.88, ~50.5% Royer devigged) and Kalshi both call this a coin flip, so the edge is thin, but it tilts Royer. Svrcina's 2-0 H2H is real yet stale and clay-only (Prostejov 2024, Barletta Apr 2025), when Royer sat around #190; Royer has since peaked at #54, made US Open R2 in 2025 (beat Bu 6-1 6-4 7-6(1) here) and won three legitimate slam R1s in best-of-five, plus a Tsitsipas retirement. Svrcina is 0-2 in 2026 slam R1s with one career slam main-draw win (2023). Bo5 on a quick NY court rewards Royer's 6'2" serve; Svrcina is 5'10", has played four matches in seven days ending with a Friday three-setter, and arrived on a three-match losing run (Droguet, Lajal, and, as defending Cancun champion, a 41-year-old Wawrinka who had not won in three months). Royer is fresher and won Kingston 5-0 on hard eight days ago. Against that: transitive chains (Wallin, Galarneau, Tirante) lean Svrcina, and Royer is only 2-11 at tour level on hard in 2026. A modest lean, not a mispricing, so no medal.

Mpetshi Perricard sits at a season-low #104 (career high #29) and has not won a match since June 14: L Bublik, L Moutet, L Hanfmann, L Trevor Svajda (#389, Cincinnati qualifying), L Brooksby 6-3 6-2 in 60 minutes — four breaks conceded, zero break points earned. TennisAbstract rates him the worst returner in the top 50 (~10% of return games broken); against a lefty holding 78.4% career and saving 62% of break points, his only route is tiebreaks, and he has lost his last several tight sets. Rodionov is #143, 8-3 over six weeks, and qualified at Flushing for the first time in five attempts by beating Fearnley (#100, above MPE) as a ~3.00 dog. Against him: three matches and two three-setters in his legs, no slam main-draw win, and a 6-1 6-4 loss to Sakamoto on hard 11 days ago. rows.analysis: US Open R1, outdoor hard, ~84F and humid. Books (1.68/2.19; 1.75/2.30) and Kalshi both sit ~57% De Jong - near fair, a shade cheap. The bear case is De Jong 0-6 at tour level on hard in 2026, but those were Medvedev, Rublev, Khachanov, Michelsen, Walton; ESPN omits that he went 2-1 at the Quebec City Challenger (outdoor hard, Aug 18-21) as 8th seed, beating Sweeny 7-5 6-0 and Budkov Kjaer 6-3 6-1, plus a Murcia hard SF in March. Passaro is live: 3-0 in qualifying without dropping a set, and #207 badly understates a career-high #89 derailed by a February wrist microlesion and his father's death in May. But he has never completed a Grand Slam main-draw win (1-3; the win was Dimitrov retiring), and his 2026 outside qualifying is thin - 4-6 0-6 to Roca Batalla, losses to Dalla Valle and Kicker. Best-of-five breaks the tie: De Jong is 2-0 in five-setters in 2026 and beat Passaro from two sets down at RG 2025, winning the fifth 6-1 in 3h49m. Common opponents lean the same way. Small edge, nothing the market has plainly missed - no medal.

rows.title: Samuel vs Machac
rows.tournament: US Open 2026 R1, outdoor hard, Flushing Meadows (Aug 30, 13:00 ET)
rows.headline: Machac 0-2, no sets won since a 79-day foot layoff; Samuel peaking and on-site
rows.analysis: US Open R1, outdoor hard, mild (~80F). Machac (#62, CH #20) tore a left foot muscle at Roland Garros, missed the entire grass swing and Wimbledon, and sat 79 days. Since returning he lost 3-6 2-6 to Carreno Busta (Cincinnati, Aug 14) and 2-6 6-7(1) to #389 Mees Rottgering (Winston-Salem, Aug 25), who had never won a tour-level match: zero sets won in two matches, his worst loss by ranking since 2023. He also retired mid-match at Montpellier in February and withdrew from Rome in May, so 2026 is a pattern of breakdowns, and best-of-five on hard is the harshest test of that foot; a retirement settles as a loss. Samuel (#110, career high this month) is at his peak: Winnipeg Challenger title in July without dropping a set, then three qualifying wins on these exact courts, two days' rest. Caveat: Machac's class is real (Adelaide title, wins over Tsitsipas, Dimitrov, Paul) and Samuel has never beaten a top-70 player in a completed match. Bookmakers 1.73/2.11 devig to 55/45, matching Kalshi exactly, so the story is priced; I sit a shade above on the fitness tail.

rows.headline: Candiotto is the class of the court, beat Romero in a final, hasn't dropped a set
rows.analysis: Two brand-new pairings, near-identical combined doubles ranks (586 vs 621), so this starts near a coin flip. Three things tip it. (1) Candiotto is the best doubles player on court - #263/CH #224, 15 career ITF titles at 22 - and is in career-best form: 7-0 and 14-0 in SETS over 11 days, including the Campos do Jordao title on Aug 22. (2) She already beat Romero in a final (Luque, Jun 20, 7-6(4) 7-5) when Romero had her stronger regular partner Moyano. (3) Route dominance on the same courts this week: Cabezas/Candiotto lost 11 games in three matches; Navarro/Romero needed two match tiebreaks and dropped two sets. Finals conversion backs it - Team A's players are 6-3 in 2026 doubles finals, Team B's 3-7, with Romero and Navarro each losing their last three. Team B's best card is Southaven (Aug 8, same W35 hard level) where Navarro/V.Rodriguez beat Cabezas 10-8 in the deciding tiebreak - but Cabezas's partner there was Tanguilig (#431), a big downgrade on Candiotto. rows.analysis: W35 Barueri SF, outdoor hard. Brace (#255, 3 seed) has been the more dominant player this week - 6-2 6-2, 6-1 6-1, 6-3 6-4, just 13 games lost - while Nana (#596, at career high) needed 1h51m to edge Victoria Barros 6-3 6-4 from 1-4 down in the second. Her level markers bracket cleanly: beats ~#345, routined 3-6 1-6 by Julia Riera (#148). Brace at #255 sits above that line. Against it: Brace is 10-15 in 2026 (7-15 before this week), slid from #182, and Nana is junior world No.7 at home in Sao Paulo with a crowd she publicly called for - which is why this isn't 75/25. Bookmakers post Brace 1.38 / Nana 2.51, devigging to ~65/35, above Kalshi's 63c ask. Nothing here is hidden from the market: a fair price with a couple of points on the favorite.

rows.title: Fery vs Buse
rows.tournament: Winston-Salem Open (ATP 250) Final, outdoor hard, Wake Forest Tennis Complex, NC — Sat 29 Aug, not before 4pm ET
rows.headline: Fery won their only meeting 6-3 6-1 on hard, is fresher, and Buse is clay-first
rows.analysis: Two players ranked #36 and #37, so a 52/48 market is honest — but three things lean Fery. (1) They have met: Fery beat Buse 6-3 6-1 in 67 minutes on indoor hard (Stockholm qualifying, 11 Oct 2025) when Fery was #230 and Buse #108 — a compact flat counterpuncher overwhelming a clay-bred topspinner. (2) Surface: Buse's 2026 tour-level hard record was 0-3 entering this week (4-3 now, all four wins here); he is the first Peruvian in an ATP hard final since 2004, and his title came on Hamburg clay. Fery is 6-3 on hard, 8-3 on grass, beat Cobolli and Dimitrov at Wimbledon and took De Minaur to 7-5 7-6(3) in Cincinnati. (3) Legs: ~5h35 on court this week vs Buse's ~8h after Duckworth's 59-minute retirement, in mid-80s humidity. Against that, Buse beat much the better field (Walton, Altmaier, JM Cerundolo, Bonzi) while Fery's half of the draw collapsed, and Buse already owns a trophy. All of this is public and priced, so no medal — but 53c is a shade cheap.

rows.headline: Fade the streak: every Zoldakova scalp was #496+, and 39c undervalues a #238 in form
rows.analysis: Market makes 18yo qualifier Zoldakova (#642) a 59-64% favorite over #238 Mikulskyte purely off a dominant week, but the run came vs #496-#800 opposition after seeds 1/4/5 exited her quarter in R1. Her record vs the top-450 band in the last 3 months is 1-3: best career win is #373 Serban (Jun), and she lost 4-6 1-6 to #434 Kovackova on Aug 19 and 4-6 4-6 to Salkova in July. Mikulskyte has faced and beaten meaningfully better players all month: WTA125 Warsaw QF (beat Kawa #~290, lost only to #184 Knutson), W75 Vitoria final in July (lost to #182 Kubka in 3), and this week ground past #280 Urgesi and #~330 Geerlings. At 39c ask vs a fair ~46-50%, Mikulskyte is the only side with value; Zoldakova at 64c requires ~70% true prob the class evidence can't support. Real counter-signals exist and cap the fade: the lone common-opponent chain (Di Girolami) favors Zoldakova, and Mikulskyte is 0-3 in 2026 vs teen ball-strikers — hence modest probability and bronze only.

rows.headline: Castelnuovo's class, serve and 21cm edge over a hot but unranked 18-year-old
rows.analysis: M25 Taipei 2 SF, outdoor hard, ~35C. Castelnuovo is #455 (CH #342 in May), a Challenger regular playing down: he won M25 Maanshan in April beating Santillan, and yesterday beat Yanki Erel (#346) 6-4 6-4, the best win either man has here. Chen has no ATP singles ranking at all ($1,815 career prize money, ITF junior #16) but is 3-0 this week without dropping a set: Matsuda 6-3 6-0, Jasika (#402) 6-4 6-3, Hyeon Chung (ex-#19, ~#500) 7-5 6-0. Those are real scalps, which is why the price is only 55/45. I discount them modestly: Jasika was on his 9th match in 16 days and third straight event, and Chung is a 30-year-old comeback veteran who folded 6-0. The structural read favours Castelnuovo: a 1.88m lefty with a one-hander serving at a 1.67m/58kg junior on hard, 29 vs 18, and at the same M25 Maanshan in April Castelnuovo took the title while Chen lost R1. Both are left-handed, so neither gets the usual lefty edge. Chen is on his fifth straight match day; Castelnuovo had 18 days rest and scratched from doubles to protect his legs. I make it ~60/40, a small edge on the 57c ask, not a mispricing worth a medal.

rows.analysis: Monterrey WTA 500 SF, outdoor hard, Friday night. Books 1.69/2.17 = Mertens ~56% de-vigged; Kalshi matches almost exactly, so there is no mispricing to exploit. H2H is 1-1 but split by surface: Mertens won the hard meeting 6-0 6-4 (AO, Jan) with 8 aces, 69% first serves and 61% of total points; Bartunkova's 6-1 6-4 win came on Berlin grass, where Mertens made 52% firsts, 7 DFs and won only 30% of second-serve points - a grass-specific serve collapse that doesn't transfer to hard. Fatigue is the live differentiator: Bartunkova has ~7h on court in five days, including back-to-back 2h45 and 2h44 wins on consecutive days, with 8 double faults and 11 break points faced against world #90 Vidmanova. Mertens has ~3h30, her QF lasting 1h28. Against the tour's best rally-extender, a leaking serve on tired legs gets punished. Against that: Bartunkova is at a career-high #38, beat Tauson and Andreescu on hard this month, and Mertens hasn't beaten a top-40 player on hard since February. But the market has already repriced Bartunkova from 3.70 to 2.17 in this exact matchup since January - her rise is priced in. Thin lean to the fresher, better hard-court server.

rows.analysis: W35 Trieste SF, outdoor clay, ~30C, no rain, no wind of note. Teixido Garcia is #358 — her career high, hit this week — and the 4 seed; Lovric is #528 (CH #405). Teixido has three completed straight-set wins here (6-2 6-3, 6-3 7-5, then 6-1 6-1 over #541 Mettraux): 36 games to 12, no set dropped. Lovric has completed exactly ONE match all week, 7-6(2) 6-2 over Vogt (#467) on Aug 24; Toth (#392, 5 seed) retired at 6-2 4-0 and Colmegna (#341, 2 seed) gave a walkover — 10 competitive games in four days. Level ceiling favours Teixido: two W35 finals in 2026 (Jackson, Casablanca) and 4-0 in semis, vs Lovric's W15 Klagenfurt title and W35 quarterfinals. Against that: books make Lovric the 1.71 favourite, she is 28-15 to 26-21, she beat Colmegna in the Klagenfurt final, Trieste sits 20km from Slovenia (home crowd, no travel), and at Prague last week she went 5-1 from qualifying while Teixido lost her opener. A genuine coin flip. I make it 52/48 Teixido; at 48c she is the only side priced under fair, while LOV at 56c is above even the sharp line.

rows.analysis: Cigarran (26, ARG, #653 career-high) looks fresher and sharper than his ranking implies: 10 days ago he won two Challenger-qualifying rounds and pushed ATP #195 Giustino to a competitive 6-4 6-3 in Sion's Challenger main draw, then rested a week before this M15 and won R1/R16 comfortably (4 of last 5 overall). Rejchtman Vinciguerra (19, SWE lefty, #879, career-high #871 from Aug 3) is a real prospect -- AO juniors QF 2025, coached by Thomas Hogstedt -- but is three straight tournament weeks into a singles-plus-doubles grind: won the Malmo M15 doubles title (Aug 15), lost the Bastad doubles final (Aug 22), then flew to Germany and lost his opening doubles rubber with a new, weaker partner. His 2026 clay record is a moderate 8-11 versus 16-13 on hard, and this event sits on his weaker surface. He's shown no visible fatigue yet (2-0 in singles here, including a gritty 7-5 1-6 7-6(5) win), so this is cumulative-load and surface risk, not a collapse call. Cigarran's recent level of competition (Challenger) has simply been higher than Rejchtman Vinciguerra's, who is 0-4 in Challenger qualifying in 2026. First meeting between the two.

rows.headline: 150 ranks higher, owns Swiss altitude clay, and Lene keeps breaking down
rows.analysis: Books price Lene 1.68 / Stusek 1.97 (vig-free 54/46), which reads as an over-reaction to one outlier week. Lene's whole case is the W100 Maspalomas run (qualified, beat Carle #231) - but three days earlier she lost a W15 QF to Shannon Lam, and that W100 run ended with her retiring at 4-4 in the third. Her baseline is W15/W35. Stusek's baseline is higher: #379 vs #526, 4-seed vs 8-seed, a W50-W100/WTA regular stepping DOWN to a W35. In July she beat Podoroska in the Hamburg WTA main draw and took a set off Korpatsch, the #46 who won that title. Conditions favour her too: her only pro title came at W35 Klosters (1,190m Swiss mountain clay) in June; Verbier is the same profile at ~1,500m, and Lene has no altitude-clay history. R16 quality splits the same way - Stusek beat a pro (U. Radwanska), Lene needed a tiebreak against a Swiss junior. Add Lene's retirement pattern and I make Stusek ~53% against a 0.48 ask. Neither plays doubles, so workload is identical: both returned from ~26 days off on Aug 26.

Cvetkovic (#920) sits 380 places below Strakhova (#542) but that number badly lags: she is ITF junior world #8, made the Roland Garros junior QF this year, and reached two ITF finals last October. She is 6-1 across two straight weeks at this venue - Verbier 1 SF, then qualifying plus two main-draw wins - giving her 7 matches of adaptation to Verbier's 1,500m altitude clay against Strakhova's 2. Strakhova is the more accomplished player and her fortnight is strong at a higher level: she qualified into the Prague W50 QF, beat 7th seed Tikhonova 6-4 6-0, and lost to top seed Havlickova only in three. Since Aug 16 she has played roughly 13 matches - Prague singles through the QF plus a doubles run to the final on Aug 22 - then travelled ~900km and 1,300m up to Verbier and restarted Aug 26, playing singles and doubles on both Aug 26 and 27, with a doubles SF again today. Gao's run to the Prague final (Aug 18-22) was HARD court at W50, included a walkover over top seed Havlickova, and her one real test she lost 6-1 6-1. Her 2026 clay record is 7-7, with three one-sided June clay losses and a 6-4 6-1 defeat to Du Pree at W25 Ourense on Aug 6 — buried outside any last-5 form view. Palicova's August was clay at W75: the Hechingen title beating Fiona Ferro (WTA ~159, ex-#39) 5-7 7-5 6-4 over 2h48m, then the Koksijde final, losing 7-5 in the third. Common opponents agree: Palicova beat Barthel 6-3 7-5 and Noha Akugue 6-2 6-4; Gao lost to Barthel 6-0 7-6(0) and retired against Noha Akugue. Style fits too — Gao is 1.80m and flat, all her best results on hard; Palicova, 1.68m, 22, and up ~100 ranking spots in three weeks, is a Czech clay grinder in her element.

rows.title: Draxl vs Schoolkate
rows.tournament: US Open qualifying final round (Q3), outdoor hard, Flushing Meadows, Court 7
rows.headline: Draxl's quallie path was far tougher; Schoolkate's Q2 win came over an 18-month-rusty PR
rows.analysis: Genuine coin flip and the market agrees: bookies 1.77/1.79 (~50/50), Kalshi 0.50/0.52. Schoolkate has the better CV -- #188 vs #216, career high 95 vs 113, $1.6M vs $718k prize money, and US Open R2 in both 2024 and 2025 with five-set wins over Taro Daniel and Sonego at this venue. Draxl has one slam main draw ever. But this week's evidence tips the other way. Draxl beat #13 seed Mejia 6-4 6-7(5) 6-4, then dismissed 17-year-old Andrew Johnson -- who had just beaten Taro Daniel from 1-4 down in the third -- 6-4 6-2. Schoolkate beat Jack Secord, then needed a tiebreak to edge Seongchan Hong, who was playing his first pro matches in 18 months after military service on a protected #147. Discount that and his form is thin: retired at Lexington as the 3 seed on Aug 4, failed to qualify at a Quebec City Challenger Aug 18. Draxl made the Winnipeg final in July, beating Mochizuki (seed 6 here) 6-0 6-3, and already converted a slam Q3 in 2026 over Mackenzie McDonald. Counterweight is real: Schoolkate beat Andrade and Sakamoto, both of whom beat Draxl. Draxl 54%.
